title.zh: 卷306 列傳九十三 曹一士 李慎修 李元直 陈​​法 胡定 仲永檀 柴潮生 储麟趾
title.en: Volume 306 Biographies 93: Cao Yishi, Li Shenxiu, Li Yuanzhi, Chen ​​Fa, Hu Ding, Zhong Yongtan, Chai Chaosheng, Chu Linzhi
title.raw: 卷306 列傳九十三 曹一士 李慎修 李元直 陈​​法 胡定 仲永檀 柴潮生 储麟趾

sentences.zh: 曹一士，字諤廷，江蘇上海人。

translations.literal: Cao Yishi, courtesy name Eting, was a native of Shanghai in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yishi, whose courtesy name was Eting, came from Shanghai in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 雍正七年進士，改庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongzheng he passed the jinshi examination, was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, and after dispersal from the academy was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongzheng he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and after completing his probation was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 十三年，考選雲南道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was selected by examination and appointed Supervising Censor of the Yunnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was chosen by examination and appointed supervising censor for the Yunnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，諭群臣更番入對。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, he instructed all officials to take turns entering for audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong came to the throne, he ordered the officials to appear before him in rotation.

sentences.zh: 一士疏言：「敬讀諭旨，曰'百姓安則朕躬安'，大哉王言，聞者皆感涕。

translations.literal: Cao Yishi memorialized, saying: 'Reverently reading the imperial rescript, which says "When the common people are at peace, then I myself am at peace"—how grand are these royal words! All who heard them were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yishi submitted a memorial: "Reading reverently the imperial rescript that says, 'When the people are secure, then I am secure'—what magnanimous words from the throne! All who heard them were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為欲百姓之安，其要莫先於慎擇督撫。

translations.literal: This humble subject considers that if one wishes the common people to be at peace, there is nothing more essential than carefully selecting governors-general and provincial governors.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes that if the people are to be kept secure, nothing matters more than choosing governors-general and provincial governors with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 督撫者守令之倡。

translations.literal: Governors-general and provincial governors are the leaders among prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Governors-general and provincial governors stand at the head of the prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 顧其中皆有賢者、有能者，賢能兼者上也，賢而不足於能者次之，能有餘而賢不足者又其次也。

translations.literal: Yet among them there are the worthy and the capable; those who combine both worthiness and capability rank highest, those who are worthy but lacking in capability come next, and those with surplus capability but insufficient worthiness rank after that.
translations.idiomatic: Among them are men of virtue and men of ability; best are those who possess both, next are the virtuous who fall short in ability, and after them come the able who lack sufficient virtue.

sentences.zh: 督撫之為賢為能，視其所舉而瞭如。

translations.literal: Whether governors-general and provincial governors are worthy or capable can be seen clearly from those they recommend.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a governor-general or provincial governor is virtuous or capable becomes perfectly clear from the men he recommends.

sentences.zh: 今督撫舉守令，約有數端：曰年力富強，曰治事勤慎，曰不避嫌怨。

translations.literal: At present, when governors-general and provincial governors recommend prefects and magistrates, there are roughly several criteria: namely strength of years and vigor, diligence and care in handling affairs, and not avoiding suspicion and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Today, when governors-general and provincial governors put forward prefects and magistrates, they rely on a few standard points: vigor of age and body, diligence and prudence in office, and willingness to face enmity without flinching.

sentences.zh: 徵其實跡，則錢糧無欠，開墾多方，善捕盜賊。

translations.literal: When one verifies their actual accomplishments, there are no arrears in taxes and grain, extensive reclamation, and skill in capturing bandits and thieves.
translations.idiomatic: When their actual record is examined, taxes and grain are paid in full, land is widely opened for cultivation, and bandits and thieves are effectively captured.

sentences.zh: 果如所言，洵所謂能吏也。

translations.literal: If truly as described, they are what may be called capable officials.
translations.idiomatic: If all this proves true, such men are indeed what people call capable officials.

sentences.zh: 乃未幾而或以贓汙著，或以殘刻聞，舉所謂貪吏、酷吏者，無一不出於能吏之中，彼誠有才以濟其惡耳。

translations.literal: Yet before long some become noted for corruption, or heard of for cruelty and harshness; the so-called greedy officials and harsh officials, not one fails to come from among capable officials—they indeed had talent to aid their wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet before long some are exposed as corrupt, others become notorious for cruelty—and every one of these greedy or harsh officials had first passed as a capable one. They truly possessed talent enough to serve their wickedness.

sentences.zh: 夫吏之賢者，悃愊無華，惻怛愛人，事上不為詭隨，吏民同聲謂之不煩。

translations.literal: As for worthy officials, they are sincere and unadorned, compassionate and loving toward people, do not act with sycophantic compliance toward superiors, and officials and common people alike call them free from trouble.
translations.idiomatic: A worthy official is plain and sincere, tender-hearted toward the people, refuses fawning compliance with his superiors, and is praised alike by colleagues and commoners as a man who governs without vexation.

sentences.zh: 度今世亦不少其人，而督撫薦剡曾未及此，毋亦輕視賢而重視能之故耶？

translations.literal: I estimate that in the present age there are also not a few such men, yet in the recommendation slips of governors-general and provincial governors they have never reached this point—is it not because they slight worthiness and emphasize capability?
translations.idiomatic: I believe the present age still has no shortage of such men, yet they scarcely appear on the recommendation lists of governors-general and provincial governors. Is this not because worthiness is undervalued while capability is over prized?

sentences.zh: 抑以能吏即賢吏耶？

translations.literal: Or do they take capable officials to be worthy officials?
translations.idiomatic: Or do they simply equate the capable official with the worthy one?

sentences.zh: 臣恐所謂能者非真能也，以趨走便利而謂之能，則老成者為遲鈍矣；

translations.literal: I fear that what is called capability is not true capability—if capability is judged by ease in running errands, then the mature and steady become sluggish and dull.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that what passes for ability is not ability at all. If quick compliance in running errands counts as ability, then seasoned and deliberate men are dismissed as slow and dull.

sentences.zh: 以應對捷給而謂之能，則木訥者為迂疏矣；

translations.literal: If capability is judged by quick and fluent responses, then the plain-spoken and slow become pedantic and remote.
translations.idiomatic: If sharp and fluent replies count as ability, then plain, reserved men are judged pedantic and obtuse.

sentences.zh: 以逞才喜事而謂之能，則鎮靜者為怠緩矣；

translations.literal: If capability is judged by showing off talent and stirring up affairs, then the calm and steady become lax and sluggish.
translations.idiomatic: If flaunting talent and courting trouble count as ability, then calm and steady men are condemned as lax and indolent.

sentences.zh: 以武健嚴酷、不恤人言而謂之能，則勞於撫字、拙於鍛鍊者謂之沽名釣譽、才力不及，而摭拾細故以罷黜之矣。

translations.literal: If capability is judged by martial vigor and harsh severity with no regard for public opinion, then those who labor at nurturing the people and are clumsy at training are called seeking fame and angling for reputation, deficient in talent and strength, and are dismissed by picking up petty matters.
translations.idiomatic: If martial harshness and contempt for public opinion count as ability, then men who wear themselves out nurturing the people and are awkward at showy exertion are called fame-seekers of insufficient talent, and are removed on trifling pretexts.

sentences.zh: 至於所取者潰敗決裂，則曰臣不合誤舉，聽部議而已。

translations.literal: As for those selected who collapse and burst apart, they say, 'Your subject failed to mis-recommend,' and leave it to the ministry to deliberate—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: When those they chose fail catastrophically, they say only, 'Your subject erred in recommendation,' and leave the matter to the ministry for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 夫有誤舉必有誤劾，誤舉如此，則誤劾者何如？

translations.literal: Where there is mistaken recommendation there must be mistaken impeachment; if mistaken recommendation is like this, then what of mistaken impeachment?
translations.idiomatic: Where recommendations go wrong, impeachments go wrong as well. If mistaken recommendation is treated so lightly, what becomes of mistaken impeachment?

sentences.zh: 誤舉者猶可議其罪，誤劾者將何從問乎？

translations.literal: Those who mistakenly recommend can still be questioned for their guilt—where is one to seek accountability for those who mistakenly impeach?
translations.idiomatic: A mistaken recommender may still be called to account, but against a mistaken impeacher where is justice to be sought?

sentences.zh: 臣以為今之督撫，明作有功之意多，而惇大成裕之道少；

translations.literal: I consider that among present governors-general and provincial governors, the intent to clearly reward merit is much, while the way of encouraging great achievement with magnanimity is little.
translations.idiomatic: I believe today's governors-general and provincial governors are far readier to reward visible achievement than to cultivate greatness through generous forbearance.

sentences.zh: 損下益上之事多，而損上益下之義少；

translations.literal: Matters of injuring those below to benefit those above are many, while the principle of injuring those above to benefit those below is little.
translations.idiomatic: They do much that harms those below to serve those above, and little that sacrifices the interests of superiors for the sake of the people.

sentences.zh: 此治體所關也。

translations.literal: This concerns the fundamental structure of governance.
translations.idiomatic: This goes to the very foundations of good government.

sentences.zh: 皇上於凡丈量開墾、割裂州縣、改調牧令，一切紛更煩擾，皆行罷革。

translations.literal: The Emperor has for all matters of surveying and measuring, reclamation, splitting prefectures and counties, and transferring pasture officials—every confused and troubling change—carried out abolition and reform.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already abolished every vexatious change—land surveys, reclamation drives, the carving up of prefectures and counties, the reassignment of pastoral officials, and the like.

sentences.zh: 為督撫者，度無不承流宣化，所慮者，彼或執其成心，飾非自護；

translations.literal: For those serving as governors-general and provincial governors, I estimate none fails to follow the flow and proclaim reform; what is feared is that they may hold to their settled views, adorn wrongs and protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: No governor-general or provincial governor can fail to echo this reforming tide; the worry is that some will cling to old habits, gloss over their faults, and shield themselves.

sentences.zh: 意為迎合，姑息偷安。

translations.literal: They act with intent to cater and appease, indulging and seeking ease.
translations.idiomatic: Some will court approval and choose indulgent ease over honest effort.

sentences.zh: 臣敢請皇上特頒諭旨，剖析開導，俾於精明嚴肅之中，布優游寬大之政。

translations.literal: I venture to request that Your Majesty specially issue an imperial rescript, analyzing and guiding, so that amid keen clarity and strictness one may deploy a policy of ease and magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to issue a special edict that analyzes and instructs them, so that within a rule both keen and strict there may also be room for a generous and humane policy.

sentences.zh: 所屬守令，敕於保題薦舉時，分列賢員、能員，然後條疏實事於下。

translations.literal: Regarding subordinate prefects and magistrates, command that at the time of securing recommendations and nominations, they separately list worthy officials and capable officials, and then set forth actual deeds below in detail.
translations.idiomatic: As for the prefects and magistrates under them, command that when securing nominations they distinguish worthy men from able men, and then set out concrete deeds in detail.

sentences.zh: 能員有敗行，許自行檢舉；

translations.literal: If capable officials have bad conduct, permit self-accusation.
translations.idiomatic: If an able man later proves corrupt, let him be allowed to confess it himself.

sentences.zh: 賢員著劣跡，則從重處分。

translations.literal: If worthy officials show bad traces, then punish heavily.
translations.idiomatic: If a worthy man is found guilty of misconduct, punish him all the more severely.

sentences.zh: 倘所舉皆能而無賢，則非大吏乏正己率屬之方，即賢者有壅於上聞之患。

translations.literal: If all recommended are capable and none worthy, then either the great officials lack methods of rectifying themselves and leading subordinates, or the worthy have the affliction of being blocked from reaching the superior's knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: If every recommendation is of the able and none of the worthy, then either the senior official lacks the discipline to govern himself and his subordinates, or worthy men are being shut out from the throne's hearing.

sentences.zh: 督撫之賢否，視所舉而瞭如矣。」

translations.literal: Whether governors-general and provincial governors are worthy or not can be seen clearly from those they recommend.'
translations.idiomatic: Whether a governor-general or provincial governor is worthy becomes perfectly clear from those he chooses to promote."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上為通諭諸督撫。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the Emperor issued a general edict to all governors-general and provincial governors.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the Emperor circulated its substance in a general edict to all governors-general and provincial governors.

sentences.zh: 一士又請寬比附妖言之獄，並禁挾仇誣告，疏言：「古者太史采詩以觀民風，藉以知列邦政治之得失、風俗之美惡，即虞書在治忽以出納五言之意，使下情之上達也。

translations.literal: Cao Yishi also requested leniency for cases of association with heterodox speech, and prohibition of lodging accusations out of enmity, memorializing: 'In antiquity the Grand Historian collected songs to observe the customs of the people, thereby knowing the gains and losses of various states' governance and the beauty or ugliness of customs—this is the meaning in the Book of Yu of attending to governance and negligence to receive and deliver the five-character edicts, enabling lower sentiments to reach upward.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yishi also asked that cases of "association with seditious speech" be treated more leniently and that malicious denunciation be forbidden. He wrote: "In antiquity the Grand Historian gathered folk songs to observe the people's customs, and so learned whether each state's government succeeded or failed and whether its manners were sound or corrupt. This is the meaning of the passage in the Book of Yu about watching over order and neglect in receiving and transmitting the people's words—it was meant to let grievances from below reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 降及周季，子產猶不禁鄉校之議。

translations.literal: Down to the late Zhou, Zichan still did not prohibit discussions at the village schools.
translations.idiomatic: Even by the late Zhou, Zichan still did not forbid the talk at the village schools.

sentences.zh: 惟是行僻而堅，言偽而辨，雖屬聞人，聖人亦必有兩觀之誅，誠恐其惑眾也。

translations.literal: Only those whose conduct is devious yet stubborn, whose words are false yet clever—though they be notorious men—the Sage would also necessarily impose the punishment of the twin platforms, truly fearing they would delude the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Only when a man's conduct was perverse and unyielding, and his words false yet artful—even if he were a public figure—would the sage ruler resort to execution at the twin platforms, truly fearing that such a man might mislead the multitude.

sentences.zh: 往者造作語言，顯有悖逆之跡，如罪人戴名世、汪景祺等，聖祖、世宗因其自蹈大逆而誅之，非得已也。

translations.literal: Formerly those who fabricated language with clearly rebellious traces, such as the criminals Dai Mingshi, Wang Jingqi, and others—Emperor Shengzu and Emperor Shizong put them to death because they themselves stepped into great rebellion; it was not without necessity.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times, men such as Dai Mingshi and Wang Jingqi, who composed language with plainly treasonous intent, were executed by the Kangxi and Yongzheng emperors because they had truly committed great rebellion—not without cause.

sentences.zh: 若夫賦詩作文，語涉疑似，如陳鵬年任蘇州知府，遊虎丘作詩，有密奏其大逆不道者，聖祖明示九卿，以為'古來誣陷善類，大率如此'。

translations.literal: As for composing poetry and essays with language touching on what seems suspicious, such as when Chen Pengnian was Suzhou prefect and composed poetry while visiting Tiger Hill, someone secretly memorialized that he was guilty of great rebellion—Emperor Shenzu clearly showed the Nine Ministers, saying, 'Since antiquity the framing of good men has largely been like this.'
translations.idiomatic: When poetry or prose merely touched on what seemed suspicious—as when Chen Pengnian, while serving as prefect of Suzhou, wrote poems on a visit to Tiger Hill, and someone secretly accused him of treason—Emperor Kangxi openly told the Nine Ministers, 'Since antiquity, the framing of good men has mostly taken this form.'

sentences.zh: 如神之哲，洞察隱微，可為萬世法。

translations.literal: Such divine wisdom, penetrating hidden subtleties, can serve as law for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Such godlike discernment, piercing hidden truth, may stand as a model for all ages.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，小人不識兩朝所以誅殛大憝之故，往往挾睚眥之怨，借影響之詞，攻訐詩文，指摘字句。

translations.literal: In recent years petty men, not understanding why the two dynasties executed and punished great villains, often harbor petty grudges, borrow words of shadow and insinuation, attack and denounce poetry and prose, and pick out phrases and characters.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years petty men, failing to understand why the two previous reigns punished great traitors, have nursed private grudges and, seizing on vague insinuations, attacked poems and essays, picking over phrases and individual characters.

sentences.zh: 有司見事風生，多方窮鞫，或致波累師生，株連親故，破家亡命，甚可憫也。

translations.literal: Officials see affairs and wind arises, exhaustively investigate in many ways, sometimes causing waves that implicate teachers and students, implicate relatives and friends, families ruined and lives lost—the pity is extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates, scenting trouble, have pursued cases relentlessly, sometimes sweeping up teachers and pupils, dragging in relatives and friends, ruining families and driving men to flight—a grievous spectacle.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為井​​田封建，不過迂儒之常談，不可以為生今反古；

translations.literal: I foolishly consider that the well-field system and feudal enfeoffment are nothing but the common talk of pedantic scholars, and cannot be taken as opposing the present and reverting to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that talk of the well-field system and feudal enfeoffment is only the stock theme of pedantic scholars, and cannot be treated as a present-day attempt to overturn the age and restore antiquity.

sentences.zh: 述懷詠史，不過詞人之習態，不可以為援古刺今。

translations.literal: Expressing feelings and chanting history are nothing but the customary habit of poets, and cannot be taken as citing antiquity to satirize the present.
translations.idiomatic: Lamentations and historical verse are merely the habitual manner of poets, and cannot be treated as covert satire on the present by appeal to the past.

sentences.zh: 即有序跋偶遺紀年，亦或草茅一時失檢，非必果懷悖逆，敢於明布篇章。

translations.literal: Even if prefaces and colophons occasionally omit chronology, it may also be a momentary lapse of care by a commoner in the fields—not necessarily truly harboring rebellion, daring to openly spread it in chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Even when a preface or colophon omits a reign title, it may be no more than a moment's carelessness by some obscure writer—not proof that he truly harbored rebellion and dared publish it openly.

sentences.zh: 使以此類悉皆比附妖言，罪當不赦，將使天下告訐不休，士子以文為戒，殊非國家義以正法、仁以包蒙之意。

translations.literal: If all such cases are treated as association with heterodox speech with unpardonable guilt, it will cause endless denunciation throughout the realm, scholars taking writing as a warning—this is far from the state's meaning of rectifying the law with righteousness and embracing the obscure with benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: If every such case were punished as unpardonable sedition, denunciation would never cease and scholars would dread the written word—far from the state's intent to uphold law through righteousness and to shelter the imperfect through mercy.

sentences.zh: 伏讀皇上諭旨，凡奏疏中從前避忌，一概掃除。

translations.literal: Humbly reading Your Majesty's rescript, all former taboos in memorials are swept away entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Reading humbly Your Majesty's recent edicts, I see that old taboos in official memorials have all been swept away.

sentences.zh: 仰見聖明廓然大度，即古敷奏采風之盛。

translations.literal: Looking up I see sage clarity and magnanimous breadth—this is the flourishing of old spreading memorials and collecting customs.
translations.idiomatic: In this I see a sage's breadth of mind—the revival of that ancient flourishing when memorials were freely submitted and popular sentiment gathered in.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂大廷之章奏尚捐忌諱，則在野之筆札焉用吹求？

translations.literal: I privately consider that if court memorials still cast aside taboos, then what need is there to scrutinize the writings of those in the wild?
translations.idiomatic: If even court memorials may now speak without fear, what need is there to hunt through the private writings of men in the provinces?

sentences.zh: 請敕下直省大吏，察從前有無此等獄案、現在不准援赦者，條列上請，以俟明旨欽定。

translations.literal: I request that orders be sent to the great officials of each province, to investigate whether there were such cases formerly and those presently not permitted to invoke amnesty, list them and submit upward, to await clear imperial command for authoritative determination.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the provincial authorities be ordered to examine whether such cases occurred in the past and whether any remain ineligible for amnesty, report them item by item, and await the throne's clear ruling.

sentences.zh: 嗣後凡有舉首文字者，苟無的確踪跡，以所告之罪依律反坐，以為挾仇誣告者戒。

translations.literal: Hereafter for all who report written words, if there are no clear and definite traces, apply the reported crime in reverse according to law, as a warning to those who lodge accusations out of enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whenever someone denounces another's writing, if no clear evidence of guilt appears, let the accuser be punished under the law for the crime he alleged—a warning to all who bear false witness out of revenge.

sentences.zh: 庶文字之累可蠲，告訐之風可息矣。」

translations.literal: Then perhaps the burden of written words can be remitted, and the wind of denunciation can cease.'
translations.idiomatic: Then the curse upon the written word may be lifted, and the epidemic of malicious accusation may be stilled."

sentences.zh: 上亦如其議。

translations.literal: The Emperor also approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved this proposal as well.

sentences.zh: 雍正間督各省開墾，督撫以是為州縣課最，頗用以厲民。

translations.literal: During Yongzheng, each province was supervised in reclamation; governors-general and provincial governors made this the criterion for evaluating prefectures and counties, often using it to pressure the people.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng, the provinces were pressed to open wasteland, and governors-general and provincial governors made reclamation the measure by which prefectures and counties were judged—often to the people's harm.

sentences.zh: 一士疏言：「開墾者所以慎重曠土，勸相農夫，本非為國家益賦起見也。

translations.literal: Cao Yishi memorialized: 'Reclamation is meant to treat wasteland with care, encourage and assist farmers—it was originally not intended to increase state revenue and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yishi memorialized: "Reclamation exists to treat idle land with care and to encourage farmers—it was never meant chiefly as a scheme to swell the state's tax revenue.

sentences.zh: 臣聞各省開墾，奉行未善，其流弊有二：一曰以熟作荒。

translations.literal: I hear that reclamation in the provinces is not well carried out; its harmful practices have two: first, treating cultivated land as wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: I am told that reclamation is poorly enforced in the provinces, and that two abuses have arisen. The first is to treat cultivated land as wasteland.

sentences.zh: 州縣承上司意旨，並未勘實荒地若干，預報畝數，邀急公之名。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties, following superior intent, without surveying how much wasteland there actually is, pre-report a mu count, inviting the name of eager public service.
translations.idiomatic: Following their superiors' wishes, prefectures and counties fail to measure the wasteland that actually exists, yet pre-report a quota of mu, thereby winning praise for public zeal.

sentences.zh: 逮明知荒地不足，即責之現在熟田，以符報額。

translations.literal: When they clearly know wasteland is insufficient, they then charge existing cultivated fields to match the reported quota.
translations.idiomatic: When they know the wasteland falls short, they simply levy the deficit against land already under cultivation so as to meet the reported figure.

sentences.zh: 小民畏官，俯首而從之，咸曰：此即新墾之荒地而已。

translations.literal: Common people fear officials, bow their heads and comply, all saying: this is merely the newly reclaimed wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: The people, fearing the magistrates, bow and submit, all agreeing to call it newly reclaimed wasteland.

sentences.zh: 一曰以荒作熟。

translations.literal: Second, treating wasteland as cultivated land.
translations.idiomatic: The second abuse is to treat wasteland as cultivated land.

sentences.zh: 荒地在河壖者，地低水溢，即成沮洳；

translations.literal: Wasteland at river banks—the land is low and water overflows, immediately becoming marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Wasteland along riverbanks lies low; when the water rises it turns at once to marsh.

sentences.zh: 在山麓者，上土下石，堅不可掘；

translations.literal: At mountain foothills, top soil over bedrock, hard and impossible to dig.
translations.idiomatic: Wasteland at the foot of hills has thin soil over rock and cannot be broken for planting.

sentences.zh: 州縣悉入報墾之數。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties all include them in reported reclamation numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet prefectures and counties count all such land in their reclamation reports.

sentences.zh: 民貧乏食，止貪官給牛種草舍，餬旦夕之口，不顧地之不可墾也。

translations.literal: People poor and lacking food only covet official provision of oxen, seed, and thatched huts, filling mouths for the moment, regardless that the land cannot be reclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Poor peasants, desperate for food, grasp at the oxen, seed, and thatched shelters the government provides, living from day to day without heed to whether the land can truly be farmed.

sentences.zh: 十年之後，民不得不報熟，官不得不昇科。

translations.literal: After ten years, the people cannot but report it cultivated, and officials cannot but raise the tax assessment.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years the peasants must declare the land cultivated, and the officials must assess tax upon it.

sentences.zh: 幸而薄收，完官不足。

translations.literal: If fortunately harvest is thin, it is insufficient to complete payment to government.
translations.idiomatic: If the harvest is meager, it will not even suffice to meet the tax.

sentences.zh: 稍遇歲歉，卒歲無資，逃亡失業之患從此起矣。

translations.literal: If slightly meeting a bad year, at year's end without resources, the affliction of flight and loss of livelihood begins from this.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of poor harvest they end the season penniless, and from this begin flight, ruin, and the loss of livelihood.

sentences.zh: 然且賦額一定，州縣不敢懸欠，督撫不敢開除，飛灑均攤諸弊，又將以熟田當之。

translations.literal: Moreover, once the tax quota is fixed, prefectures and counties dare not leave arrears suspended, governors-general and provincial governors dare not cancel exemption—the abuses of spreading assessment and equal apportionment will again use cultivated fields to cover them.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, once the tax quota is fixed, prefectures and counties dare not leave arrears on the books and governors-general and provincial governors dare not grant relief; the old abuses of shifting burdens and spreading levies will again fall upon land already under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 是名為開墾，有墾之名無墾之實也。

translations.literal: This is called reclamation—in name there is reclamation but in reality there is none.
translations.idiomatic: This is what passes for reclamation: the name exists, but the reality does not.

sentences.zh: 茲二弊者，緣有司但求地利，罔惜貽害；

translations.literal: These two abuses arise because officials only seek land profit, heedless of leaving harm.
translations.idiomatic: These two abuses arise because local officials care only for land revenue and give no thought to the harm they leave behind.

sentences.zh: 大吏惟知慮始，不暇圖終；

translations.literal: Great officials only know to consider the beginning, with no leisure to plan the end.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials think only of starting the work and never of how it will end.

sentences.zh: 是以仁民之政，反啟累民之階。

translations.literal: Thus policy that should benefit the people instead opens steps that burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: Thus a policy meant to bless the people becomes instead a ladder by which they are burdened.

sentences.zh: 臣請敕下直省督撫，凡開墾地畝，無論已未昇科，俱令州縣官覆勘，內有熟田混報開墾，舉首除額，免其處分；

translations.literal: I request orders sent to provincial governors-general and governors, that for all reclaimed land mu, whether already raised in tax assessment or not, all command prefectural and county officials to re-survey; where cultivated land is mixed in reported as reclamation, report and remove from quota, exempt them from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the provincial governors-general and governors be ordered: for all reclaimed acreage, whether already taxed or not, let prefectural and county officials re-survey it. Where cultivated land has been falsely reported as reclaimed, let it be reported and struck from the quota, and let the officials be exempted from punishment.

sentences.zh: 如實為新墾，具印結存案，少有虛偽，發覺從重治罪：則以熟作荒之弊可免矣。

translations.literal: If truly newly reclaimed, provide sealed certification kept on file—slight falsity, upon discovery punish heavily: then the abuse of treating cultivated as wasteland can be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: If the land is truly new reclamation, let a sealed certificate be filed; the slightest falsification, once discovered, shall be heavily punished. Then the abuse of treating cultivated land as wasteland may be prevented.

sentences.zh: 新墾應昇科，督撫遴員覆勘，磽確瘠薄，即與免賦；

translations.literal: For newly reclaimed land due for tax raise, governors-general and provincial governors select officials to re-survey—if barren, stony, and thin, immediately grant tax exemption.
translations.idiomatic: When newly reclaimed land is due for taxation, let governors-general and provincial governors send officials to re-survey it; if the soil is stony, barren, and thin, exempt it at once.

sentences.zh: 倘因報墾在先，必令起賦，以貽民累，發覺從重治罪；

translations.literal: If because reclamation was reported first they must require tax assessment, to leave the people burdened, upon discovery punish heavily.
translations.idiomatic: If, because reclamation was reported earlier, officials nevertheless impose tax and thereby burden the people, let them, once discovered, be punished severely.

sentences.zh: 則以荒作熟之弊亦可免矣。」

translations.literal: Then the abuse of treating wasteland as cultivated can also be avoided.'
translations.idiomatic: Then the abuse of treating wasteland as cultivated land may also be prevented."

translations.literal: (Close of memorial quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of memorial.)

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，遷工科給事中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was transferred to Supervising Censor of the Office of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he was transferred to supervising censor in the Office of Works.

sentences.zh: 故事，御史遷給事中，較資俸深淺。

translations.literal: By precedent, when censors transfer to supervising censors, seniority in rank and years of service is compared.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, when censors were promoted to supervising censors, precedence was determined by seniority of rank and service.

sentences.zh: 一士入台僅六月，出上特擢。

translations.literal: Cao Yishi had entered the censorate only six months—it was a special promotion by the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yishi had served in the censorate only six months; his appointment was a special elevation by the throne.

sentences.zh: 尋疏劾原任河東河道總督王士俊，疏未下，語聞於外。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized impeaching Wang Shijun, former Governor-General of the East Yellow River, before the memorial was issued the contents leaked outside.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he memorialized to impeach Wang Shijun, the former governor-general of the Eastern Yellow River Directorate; before the memorial was issued, word of it leaked abroad.

sentences.zh: 上疑一士自洩之，召對詰責，下吏議，當左遷，仍命寬之。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected Cao Yishi had leaked it himself, summoned him for audience and interrogated him, referred to officials for deliberation—sentence was demotion, yet the Emperor still ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor suspected that Cao Yishi himself had leaked it, summoned him for questioning, and referred the matter for official deliberation, which recommended demotion; the Emperor nevertheless showed mercy.

sentences.zh: 一士复疏請復六科舊職，​​專司封駁，巡視城倉、漕鹽等差，皆不當與。

translations.literal: Cao Yishi again memorialized requesting restoration of the six departments' old duties, exclusively handling review and rejection; inspection of city granaries, transport grain, salt, and other assignments were all inappropriate to share.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yishi again memorialized asking that the six departments be restored to their old duties of reviewing and rejecting memorials, and that they no longer be burdened with inspecting city granaries, transport grain, salt, and the like.

sentences.zh: 又疏論各省工程報銷諸弊，請敕凡有營造開濬，以所須物料工匠遵例估定，榜示工作地方。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on abuses in provincial engineering expense reports, requesting that for all construction and dredging, required materials and craftsmen be estimated according to regulations and posted at the work site.
translations.idiomatic: He also exposed abuses in provincial engineering accounts and asked that for every construction or dredging project the required materials and labor be estimated by regulation and publicly posted at the work site.

sentences.zh: 又疏論州縣官讞獄，胥吏上下其手，竄改獄詞，請飭申禁。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on prefectural and county trials, where clerks manipulated matters and altered testimony, requesting strict prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke of trials in the prefectures and counties, where clerks manipulated proceedings and altered testimony, and asked that this be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 又疏論鹽政諸弊，請毋令商人公捐，禁司鹽官吏與商人交結；

translations.literal: He also memorialized on salt administration abuses, requesting not to allow merchants' public contributions, and prohibiting salt officials from associating with merchants.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed abuses in the salt administration, asking that merchants no longer be compelled to make public contributions and that salt officials be forbidden to collude with them.

sentences.zh: 小民肩挑背負，戒毋苛捕；

translations.literal: Common people carrying on shoulder poles and backs—warn against harsh arrest.
translations.idiomatic: As for common people carrying salt on shoulder poles and in packs, he warned against harsh arrests.

sentences.zh: 大商以便鹽船阻通行水道，戒毋堵截。

translations.literal: Large merchants using convenient salt boats to block navigable waterways—warn against obstructing and intercepting.
translations.idiomatic: As for great merchants who used privileged salt boats to choke the waterways, he warned against blocking and seizing passage.

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All these proposals were referred to the ministries for deliberation and enactment.

sentences.zh: 一士病哽噎，即以是年卒。

translations.literal: Cao Yishi suffered from choking in the throat, and in that same year died.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yishi was stricken with a choking illness of the throat and died that same year.

sentences.zh: 一士晚達，在言官未一歲，而所建白皆有益於民生世道，朝野傳誦。

translations.literal: Cao Yishi rose late in life; as a remonstrating official not yet one year, yet all his proposals benefited people's livelihood and the moral order of the age—court and countryside passed them around in recitation.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yishi had risen late in life; he served as a remonstrating official for less than a year, yet every proposal he made served the people's welfare and the health of public morals, and his words were repeated throughout court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 聞其卒，皆重惜之。

translations.literal: When they heard of his death, all deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: When news of his death spread, all mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 李慎修，字思永，山東章丘人。

translations.literal: Li Shenxiu, courtesy name Siyong, was a native of Zhangqiu in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenxiu, whose courtesy name was Siyong, came from Zhangqiu in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十一年進士，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷主事，出為浙江杭州知府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Department Director, then went out as Prefect of Hangzhou in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to department director, then sent out to serve as prefect of Hangzhou in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，入為刑部郎中，歷十餘年，治獄多所平反。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he entered service as Department Director in the Ministry of Justice; over more than ten years, in handling cases he reversed many wrongful judgments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he returned to the capital as a department director in the Ministry of Justice; over more than ten years he handled cases and reversed many wrongful verdicts.

sentences.zh: 有侵帑獄，初議以挪移從末減，慎修執不可；

translations.literal: There was a case of embezzling treasury funds; initial deliberation proposed leniency for misappropriation from the lesser penalty—Shenxiu insisted it could not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: In one case of embezzlement from the public treasury, the initial recommendation was to apply the lesser penalty for misappropriation; Shenxiu refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 或諷以上意，亦不為動。

translations.literal: Some also satirized him with hints of the emperor's intent, yet he was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: Some even tried to needle him with hints of the emperor's displeasure, but he would not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，出為河南南汝光道，移湖北武漢黃德道，以憂去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign, he went out to serve as intendant of the Nanru Guang Circuit in Henan, was transferred to the Wuhan Huangde Circuit in Hubei, and left office to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he was posted as intendant of Henan's Nanru Guang Circuit, then transferred to Hubei's Wuhan Huangde Circuit, and resigned to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，授江南驛鹽道。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he was appointed intendant of the Jiangnan Postal and Salt Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he was appointed intendant of the Jiangnan Postal and Salt Circuit.

sentences.zh: 引見，高宗曰：「李慎修老成直爽，宜言官。」

translations.literal: When he was presented to the throne, Gaozong said, "Li Shenxiu is steady and forthright; he is suited to be a remonstrating official."
translations.idiomatic: When he was presented at court, the Qianlong Emperor said, "Li Shenxiu is seasoned and bluntly honest; he is fit to serve as a remonstrating official."

sentences.zh: 特除江西道監察御史。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed supervising censor of the Jiangxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed supervising censor of the Jiangxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 疏論戶部變亂錢法，苛急煩碎。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial criticizing the Board of Revenue for overturning the coinage laws in ways that were harsh, urgent, and tediously minute.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he denounced the Board of Revenue for disordering the currency system with policies that were severe, rushed, and needlessly burdensome.

sentences.zh: 歷舉前代利害，並言錢值將騰貴，窮極其弊。

translations.literal: He cited benefit and harm from previous dynasties in turn, and also stated that the value of cash would rise sharply, exhaustively exposing the evils.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed earlier dynasties' gains and losses point by point, warned that coin would soon grow scarce and costly, and laid bare the harm to the last degree.

sentences.zh: 上元夜，賜諸王大臣觀煙火，慎修上疏諫，以為玩物喪志。

translations.literal: On the night of the Lantern Festival, the emperor granted the princes and ministers a display of fireworks; Shenxiu submitted a memorial of remonstrance, holding that indulgence in playthings destroys one's resolve.
translations.idiomatic: On Lantern Festival night the emperor treated the princes and senior ministers to fireworks; Shenxiu remonstrated in a memorial, arguing that chasing amusements blunts the will to govern.

sentences.zh: 上喜為詩，嘗召對，問能詩否，因進言：「皇上一日萬幾，恐以文翰妨政治，祈不以此勞聖慮。」

translations.literal: The emperor delighted in composing poetry; he once summoned Shenxiu for audience and asked whether he could write poetry, whereupon Shenxiu offered: "Your Majesty's daily business is myriad; I fear that literary pursuits may obstruct governance—I beg that this not weary Your Majesty's concern."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved to write poetry; once, in private audience, he asked whether Shenxiu wrote verse, and Shenxiu replied: "Your Majesty's desk holds ten thousand matters; I fear that brushwork might distract you from statecraft—please do not let poetry tax your mind."

sentences.zh: 上韙之，載其言於詩。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and recorded his words in a poem.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and worked his words into a poem.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂慎修曰：「是何眇小丈夫，乃能直言若此？」

translations.literal: He once said to Shenxiu: "What kind of insignificant fellow are you, that you can speak so bluntly?"
translations.idiomatic: He once asked Shenxiu: "What puny man are you, to speak so plainly?"

sentences.zh: 慎修對曰：「臣面陋而心善。」

translations.literal: Shenxiu replied: "Your subject's face is ugly but his heart is good."
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu answered: "I am homely of face but sound of heart."

sentences.zh: 上為大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed heartily.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor burst out laughing.

sentences.zh: 復出為湖南衡郴永道。

translations.literal: He was again sent out as intendant of the Hengchen Yong Circuit in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted again as intendant of Hunan's Heng-Chen-Yong circuit.

sentences.zh: 十二年，乞病歸，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he asked to retire for illness, went home, and died.

sentences.zh: 高密李元直為御史在其前，以剛直著。

translations.literal: Li Yuanzhi of Gaomi had served as censor before him and was noted for his uncompromising integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanzhi of Gaomi had been a censor earlier and was famed for blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 慎修與齊名，為「山東二李」。

translations.literal: Shenxiu was equally famed with him, and the two were called "the Two Lis of Shandong."
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu shared his renown; together they were known as "the Two Lis of Shandong."

sentences.zh: 京師稱元直「戇李」，慎修「短李」。

translations.literal: In the capital Yuanzhi was called "Stubborn Li" and Shenxiu "Short Li."
translations.idiomatic: Beijing nicknamed Yuanzhi "Stubborn Li" and Shenxiu "Short Li."

sentences.zh: 元直，字象山。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi, courtesy name Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi, whose courtesy name was Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年進士，改庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination, was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, and after dispersal from the academy was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 52 he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and after leaving the academy was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 雍正七年，考選四川道監察御史，八閱月，章數十上。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongzheng he was selected by examination and appointed Supervising Censor of the Sichuan Circuit; within eight months he submitted dozens of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 7 he won appointment by examination as supervising censor for the Sichuan circuit; in eight months he filed dozens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 嘗歷詆用事諸大臣，謂：「朝廷都俞多，籲咈少，有堯、舜，無皋、夔。」

translations.literal: He once repeatedly denounced the powerful ministers of the day, saying: "In court there is much assent and little dissent—we have Yao and Shun but no Gao or Kui."
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly attacked the men then in power, declaring: "The court hears too much agreement and too little frank objection—we have Yao and Shun on the throne but no Gao or Kui at their side."

sentences.zh: 上不懌，召所論列諸大臣大學士硃軾、張廷玉輩並及元直，詰之曰：「有是君必有是臣。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; he summoned the ministers Yuanzhi had named, including Grand Secretaries Zhu Shi and Zhang Tingyu, along with Yuanzhi himself, and questioned them: "Such a ruler must have such ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense. He called in the officials Yuanzhi had named—Grand Secretaries Zhu Shi and Zhang Tingyu among them—and Yuanzhi as well, and demanded: "Every ruler finds the ministers he deserves.

sentences.zh: 果如汝所言無皋、夔，朕又安得為堯、舜乎？」

translations.literal: If truly, as you say, there are no Gao or Kui, how then could I be Yao or Shun?"
translations.idiomatic: If, as you claim, there are no Gao or Kui here, how could I count myself Yao or Shun?"

sentences.zh: 元直抗論不撓，上謂諸大臣曰：「彼言雖野，心乃無他。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhi argued forcefully without yielding; the emperor told the ministers: "His words are crude, but his heart holds no other intent."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi stood his ground. The emperor told the others: "His language is rough, but his loyalty is plain."

sentences.zh: 次日，復召入，獎其敢言。

translations.literal: The next day he summoned Yuanzhi in again and praised his daring to speak.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he recalled Yuanzhi and praised his courage in speaking out.

sentences.zh: 會廣東貢荔枝至，以數枚賜之。

translations.literal: When tribute lychees arrived from Guangdong, he bestowed several upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong sent lychees as tribute, the emperor gave him a few.

sentences.zh: 未幾，命巡視台灣，疏請增養廉、絕饋遺，併條上​​番民利病數十事。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to inspect Taiwan; he memorialized asking to increase integrity-nurture allowances and cut off gifts, and also submitted several dozen items on the welfare and ills of the aboriginal population.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent to inspect Taiwan. He asked for higher "integrity nurture" stipends and an end to gift-giving, and listed several dozen measures for aboriginal welfare.

sentences.zh: 台灣居海外，巡視御史至，每自視如客，事一聽於道府。

translations.literal: Taiwan lies beyond the sea; when an inspecting censor arrived, he usually regarded himself as a guest and left all affairs to the circuit intendant and prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan sat overseas; visiting censors often acted like guests and let the circuit intendant and prefect decide everything.

sentences.zh: 元直悉反所為，時下所屬問民疾苦。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi completely reversed this practice, constantly sending his subordinates to inquire into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi did the opposite, repeatedly dispatching subordinates to ask after the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 欲有所施措，督撫劾其侵官，遂鐫級去。

translations.literal: When he wished to take action, the governor-general and governor impeached him for overstepping his office, and he was demoted and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When he tried to act, the governor-general and governor accused him of encroaching on their authority; he was demoted and removed.

sentences.zh: 家居二十餘年，卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for more than twenty years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He spent more than twenty years at home and died.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗曰：「元直可保其不愛錢，但慮任事過急。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong once said: "One can guarantee that Yuanzhi does not love money, but I worry that he is too urgent in executing affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor once said: "I can trust Yuanzhi not to crave money, but I fear he presses too hard in office."

sentences.zh: 又嘗諭諸大臣曰：「甚矣才之難得！

translations.literal: He also once instructed the ministers: "How hard it is to obtain talent!
translations.idiomatic: He also told his ministers: "How rare real talent is!

sentences.zh: 元直豈非真任事人？

translations.literal: Is Yuanzhi not truly a man who gets things done?
translations.idiomatic: Is Yuanzhi not exactly the sort who delivers results?

sentences.zh: 乃剛氣逼人太甚。」

translations.literal: Yet his overbearing rigidity presses too hard upon others."
translations.idiomatic: Yet his blunt force overwhelms people."

sentences.zh: 元直晚年言及知遇，輒泣下。

translations.literal: In his later years, whenever Yuanzhi spoke of the grace he had received, he would weep.
translations.idiomatic: In old age, whenever Yuanzhi recalled the emperor's favor, he wept.

sentences.zh: 初在翰林，與孫嘉淦、謝濟世、陳法交，以古義相勗，時稱四君子。

translations.literal: Early in the Hanlin he associated with Sun Jiagan, Xie Jishi, and Chen Fa, encouraging one another in classical righteousness; at the time they were called the Four Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: As a young Hanlin scholar he befriended Sun Jiagan, Xie Jishi, and Chen Fa, urging one another to live by ancient standards; people called them the Four Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 及嘉淦總督湖廣，治濟世獄，徇巡撫許容意，為時論所不直，元直遂與疏焉。

translations.literal: When Jiagan became governor-general of Huguang and handled the case of Jishi, siding with Governor Xu Rong in a way public opinion did not uphold, Yuanzhi thereupon distanced himself from him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jiagan governed Huguang and tried Xie Jishi's case while bending toward Governor Xu Rong—conduct critics rejected—Yuanzhi broke with him.

sentences.zh: 法，字定齋，貴州安平人。

translations.literal: Chen Fa, courtesy name Dingzhai, was a native of Anping in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fa, whose courtesy name was Dingzhai, came from Anping in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年進士，自檢討官至直隸大名道。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination; from Reviewer he rose to Intendant of Daming Circuit in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Kangxi 52, he rose from reviewer to intendant of Daming circuit in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 講學宗硃子，著明辨錄，辨陸、王之失。

translations.literal: In lecturing he took Zhu Xi as master; he authored the Mingbianlu, clarifying the errors of Lu Jiuyuan and Wang Yangming.
translations.idiomatic: He taught in the Zhu Xi tradition and wrote the Mingbianlu, refuting Lu and Wang.

sentences.zh: 蒞政以教養為先，手治文告，辭意懇摯。

translations.literal: When he took up governance he put nurture and instruction first; he personally drafted proclamations, their wording earnest and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: In office he put teaching and nurturing the people first, drafting every notice himself in language that was warm and plain.

sentences.zh: 既久，人猶誦之。

translations.literal: Long afterward people still recited them.
translations.idiomatic: Years later people still quoted them from memory.

sentences.zh: 胡定，字登賢，廣東保昌人。

translations.literal: Hu Ding, courtesy name Dengxian, was a native of Baochang in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ding, whose courtesy name was Dengxian, came from Baochang in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年進士，改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng he passed the jinshi examination, was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, and was appointed Reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 11 he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed reviewer.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五年，考選陝西道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianlong he was selected by examination and appointed Supervising Censor of the Shaanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 5 he won appointment by examination as supervising censor for the Shaanxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 七年，湖南巡撫許容劾糧道謝濟世，下湖廣總督孫嘉淦按治，將坐濟世罪，八年二月，定疏陳容陷濟世、嘉淦袒容狀，錄湖南民揭帖，謂布政使張璨、按察使王玠、長沙知府張琳、衡州通判方國寶、善化知縣樊德貽承容指，朋謀傾陷；

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Hunan Governor Xu Rong impeached Grain Intendant Xie Jishi; the case was referred to Huguang Governor-General Sun Jiagan for investigation, and Jishi was about to be convicted; in the second month of the eighth year Ding memorialized, setting forth how Rong had framed Jishi and Jiagan had shielded Rong, copying out Hunan people's placards accusing Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhang Can, Surveillance Commissioner Wang Jie, Changsha Prefect Zhang Lin, Hengzhou Sub-prefect Fang Guobao, and Shanhua Magistrate Fan Deyi of acting at Rong's direction in a clique to ruin Jishi;
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 7, Hunan governor Xu Rong impeached grain intendant Xie Jishi; Huguang governor-general Sun Jiagan was ordered to investigate and was poised to convict Jishi. In the second month of Qianlong 8, Hu Ding memorialized, detailing Rong's frame-up and Jiagan's partiality, and appended Hunan placards naming provincial administration commissioner Zhang Can, surveillance commissioner Wang Jie, Changsha prefect Zhang Lin, Hengzhou sub-prefect Fang Guobao, and Shanhua magistrate Fan Deyi as Rong's accomplices in a conspiracy to destroy Jishi;

sentences.zh: 並述京師民諺，目容為媼，謂其妒賢嫉能如婦人之陰毒。

translations.literal: He also quoted a Beijing folk saying that called Rong an old woman, saying she was jealous of the able and vicious as a woman's hidden poison.
translations.idiomatic: He also cited a Beijing rhyme that mocked Rong as a shrew, jealous of talent and spiteful as a woman's secret malice.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上命戶部侍郎阿里袞如湖南會嘉淦覆勘，並令定從往。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor ordered Vice Minister of Revenue Arigun to proceed to Hunan jointly to re-investigate with Jiagan, and also ordered Ding to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor sent Vice Minister of Revenue Arigun to Hunan to reinvestigate with Jiagan and told Ding to go along.

sentences.zh: 會湖南嶽常道倉德密揭都察院，發璨請託私改文牘狀，阿里袞至湖南，雪濟世枉。

translations.literal: At the same time Yuechang Circuit Intendant Cang De secretly memorialized the Censorate, exposing Can's request for favors and private alteration of documents; when Arigun reached Hunan, Jishi's wrongful conviction was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yuechang circuit intendant Cang De secretly reported to the Censorate that Zhang Can had solicited favors and altered documents; once Arigun reached Hunan, Jishi was vindicated.

sentences.zh: 上奪嘉淦、容等職，諭謂：「定為言官，言事不實，自有應得之罪譴。

translations.literal: The emperor stripped Jiagan, Rong, and others of their posts and instructed: "Ding serves as a remonstrating official; if his report were untrue he would deserve the appropriate punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Jiagan, Rong, and others and said: "Hu Ding speaks as a censor; if he had lied, he would deserve punishment.

sentences.zh: 今既實矣，若止為濟世白冤抑，其事尚小；

translations.literal: Now that it has proved true, if he had merely cleared Jishi's name the matter would still be small;
translations.idiomatic: Now that it is true, merely exonerating Jishi would be a small thing;

sentences.zh: 因此察出督撫等挾私誣陷，徇隱扶同，使人人知所儆戒，此則有裨於政治，為益良多。

translations.literal: but because it has exposed governors and governors-general who framed others from private motives and concealed wrongdoing in collusion, so that all may know what to fear, this greatly benefits governance and does much good.
translations.idiomatic: but because it exposes governors and governor-generals who lied from private grudges and covered for one another, warning everyone— that truly strengthens government and does great good.

sentences.zh: 至諸行省督撫舉劾必悉秉公心，方為不負委任，若以愛憎為舉劾，如嘉淦、容居心行事，豈不抱媿大廷，負慚夙夜？

translations.literal: In every province governors and governors-general in recommending and impeaching must all uphold an impartial heart—only then do they fulfill their commission; if they recommend and impeach according to love and hatred, like Jiagan and Rong in mind and conduct, how can they not feel shame before the court and remorse day and night?
translations.idiomatic: Every governor and governor-general must recommend and impeach with a fair mind or fail the trust placed in him; if favor and spite drive such decisions, as with Jiagan and Rong, how can they face the court without shame?

sentences.zh: 諸督撫當深自儆省，以嘉淦、容為戒。」

translations.literal: All governors and governors-general should deeply examine themselves and take Jiagan and Rong as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: Let every governor and governor-general take warning from Jiagan and Rong and examine himself."

sentences.zh: 定於是負敢言名。

translations.literal: Ding thereby gained a reputation for daring to speak.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Ding was famed for bold speech.

sentences.zh: 轉兵科給事中，巡視西城。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs and inspected the Western City.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs and inspected the Western City ward.

sentences.zh: 求居民善惡著稱者，皆榜姓名於衢。

translations.literal: He sought out residents of good or ill repute and posted their names on placards in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: He identified residents praised or notorious for their conduct and posted their names on public boards.

sentences.zh: 民有訟者，即時傳訊判結。

translations.literal: When the people had lawsuits, he immediately summoned the parties, questioned them, and decided the case.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners brought disputes, he summoned them at once, heard them, and ruled on the spot.

sentences.zh: 西山臥佛寺被竊，同官誤以僧自盜奏，定廉得真盜，僧得雪。

translations.literal: When Wofo Temple on the Western Hills was robbed, a colleague mistakenly memorialized that the monks had stolen from themselves; Ding investigated and found the real thieves, and the monks were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: After thieves struck Wofo Temple in the Western Hills, a colleague wrongly reported that the monks had staged the theft; Ding traced the real culprits and cleared the monks.

sentences.zh: 旋以母老乞歸養。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on grounds of his mother's age, he requested leave to return and support her.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to retire and care for his aged mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，复授福建道御史。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he was again appointed Supervising Censor of the Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was reappointed supervising censor for the Fujian circuit.

sentences.zh: 疏論內務府郎中某朘民為私利，按治事不實，奪職下刑部，久之讞定，罷歸。

translations.literal: He memorialized that a director in the Imperial Household Department had squeezed the people for private profit; the investigation proved unfounded, he was stripped of office and handed to the Ministry of Punishments, and after a long deliberation he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He charged an Imperial Household director with extorting the public; the inquiry found no basis, he lost his post and was sent to the Ministry of Punishments, and after a long trial was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，上南巡，定迎駕杭州，復原銜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when the emperor toured the south, Ding met the imperial progress at Hangzhou and his original rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 22, when the emperor traveled south, Ding greeted him at Hangzhou and regained his former rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 著有雙柏廬文集。

translations.literal: He authored the Shuangbailu Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings survive as the Shuangbailu Collection.

sentences.zh: 仲永檀，字襄西，山東濟寧人。

translations.literal: Zhong Yongtan, courtesy name Xiangxi, was a native of Jining in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yongtan, whose courtesy name was Xiangxi, came from Jining in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年進士，改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, and was appointed Reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Qianlong 1, he entered the Hanlin as a bachelor and was appointed reviewer.

sentences.zh: 五年，考選陝西道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was selected by examination and appointed Supervising Censor of the Shaanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 5 he won appointment by examination as supervising censor for the Shaanxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 疏請酌減上元燈火聲樂，略言：「人君一日萬幾，一有暇逸之心，即啟怠荒之漸。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that the Lantern Festival fireworks and music be suitably reduced, briefly stating: "A ruler's daily business is myriad; once the heart turns toward leisure, the slope toward neglect opens.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Lantern Festival fireworks and music be trimmed, writing in brief: "A ruler faces ten thousand tasks; the moment he indulges ease, slackness begins.

sentences.zh: 每歲上元前後，燈火聲樂，日有進禦。

translations.literal: Every year before and after the Lantern Festival, fireworks and music are daily presented to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Each year around the festival, fireworks and music are daily brought before the throne.

sentences.zh: 原酌量裁減，豫養清明之體。」

translations.literal: I ask that they be measured and cut back, beforehand nurturing a clear and sober constitution."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be scaled back, so as to preserve a clear and disciplined body and mind."

sentences.zh: 上降旨，謂：「書云'不役耳目'，詩云'好樂無荒'，古聖賢垂訓，朕所夙夜兢兢而不敢忽者。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a rescript, saying: "The Documents say, 'Do not enslave the ears and eyes'; the Odes say, 'Love pleasure but do not wander into excess'—such admonitions from the ancient sages are what I nightly regard with awe and dare not neglect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "The Documents warn, 'Do not enslave ear and eye'; the Odes warn, 'Enjoy pleasure but never to excess'—these teachings of the sages I ponder nightly and dare not ignore.

sentences.zh: 惟是歲時宴賞，慶典自古有之，況元正獻歲，外籓蒙古朝覲有不可缺之典禮。

translations.literal: Yet seasonal feasts and rewards are celebrations anciently established; moreover, at the New Year when the year is offered, the tributary Mongols from beyond the frontier attend court in an indispensable rite.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal feasts are ancient custom; at New Year, when the year is presented, Mongol tributaries from beyond the frontier must attend rites that cannot be omitted.

sentences.zh: 朕踵舊制而行之，未嘗有所增益。

translations.literal: I follow the old institutions in carrying them out and have never added to them.
translations.idiomatic: I follow old practice and have added nothing.

sentences.zh: 至於國家政事，朕仍如常綜理，並未略有稽遲。

translations.literal: As for state affairs, I still manage them as usual and have not in the least fallen behind.
translations.idiomatic: State business I handle as always; nothing has slipped.

sentences.zh: 永檀胸有所見，直陳無隱，是其可嘉處，朕亦知之。」

translations.literal: Yongtan speaks from conviction and states it without concealment—that is what is commendable in him, and I know it."
translations.idiomatic: Yongtan speaks what he believes without hiding it—that is what I commend in him, and I know his heart."

translations.literal: (Close of imperial rescript.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of rescript.)

sentences.zh: 京師民俞君弼者，為工部鑿匠，富無子。

translations.literal: In the capital there was a commoner named Yu Junbi, a stonemason of the Board of Works, wealthy and without sons.
translations.idiomatic: In Beijing a Board of Works stonemason named Yu Junbi was rich and childless.

sentences.zh: 既死，其戚許秉義謀爭產。

translations.literal: After he died, his kinsman Xu Bingyi plotted to contest the estate.
translations.idiomatic: After his death a relative, Xu Bingyi, schemed to seize the property.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士許王猷與同族，囑招九卿會其喪，示聲氣，且首君弼有藏鏹。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xu Wangyou was of the same clan; he arranged to summon the Nine Ministers to the funeral, displaying influence, and moreover asserted first that Junbi had hidden silver.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xu Wangyou, a clansman, had the Nine Ministers summoned to the funeral to show clout and first claimed Junbi had hoarded silver.

sentences.zh: 步軍統領鄂善以聞，詔嚴鞫，秉義論罪如律，並奪王猷職，旨戒飭九卿。

translations.literal: Stepping Commandant E Shan reported this; the emperor ordered a strict inquiry; Bingyi was sentenced according to law, Wangyou was also stripped of office, and an edict admonished the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Stepping Commandant E Shan reported it; the emperor ordered a stern investigation; Bingyi was punished by law, Wangyou was dismissed, and the Nine Ministers were rebuked by edict.

sentences.zh: 六年，永檀奏：「風聞鄂善受俞氏賄萬金，禮部侍郎吳家駒赴吊得其貲；

translations.literal: In the sixth year Yongtan memorialized: "I have heard on rumor that E Shan accepted ten thousand taels of gold in bribes from the Yu family, and that Vice Minister of Rites Wu Jiaju received part of that wealth when he attended the mourning;
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 6, Yongtan reported: "Rumor says E Shan took ten thousand taels in bribes from the Yu family, and that Vice Minister of Rites Wu Jiaju received a share when he attended the funeral;

sentences.zh: 又聞赴吊不僅九卿，大學士張廷玉以柬往，徐本、趙國麟俱親會，詹事陳浩為奔走，謹據實密奏，備訪查。」

translations.literal: I also hear that those who attended the mourning were not only the Nine Ministers—Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu sent a note, Xu Ben and Zhao Guolin both came in person, and Junior Mentor Chen Hao ran errands; I respectfully memorialize in secret according to what I know, prepared for investigation."
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that mourners were not only the Nine Ministers—Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu sent a note, Xu Ben and Zhao Guolin came in person, and junior mentor Chen Hao ran messages; I report this secretly as I know it, ready for inquiry."

sentences.zh: 又言：「密奏留中事，外間旋得消息，此必有私通左右暗為宣洩者。

translations.literal: He also said: "Matters memorialized in secret and kept within the palace soon become known outside—there must be someone privately communicating with those close to the throne who secretly leaks them.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Secret memorials kept at court still leak outside—someone must be whispering to those near the emperor.

sentences.zh: 權要有耳目，朝廷將不復有耳目矣。」

translations.literal: When the powerful have ears, the court will no longer have ears."
translations.idiomatic: If the mighty have spies, the throne will be deaf."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上疑永檀妄言，命怡親王，和親王，大學士鄂爾泰、張廷玉、徐本，尚書訥親、來保按治，摘永檀奏宣洩密奏留中果何事，又謂權要私通左右，此時無可私通之左右，亦無能私通左右之權要，詰何所見，命直陳。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor suspected Yongtan's words were reckless and ordered Prince Yi, Prince He, Grand Secretaries Ortai, Zhang Tingyu, and Xu Ben, and Ministers Neqin and Laibao to investigate; they were to press Yongtan on which secret memorial kept within the palace he claimed had been leaked, and on his charge that the powerful privately communicated with those close to the throne—at this time there were no such close attendants to communicate with privately, nor any powerful men who could privately communicate with them—and to ask on what he based this, commanding him to state it plainly.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor doubted Yongtan and ordered Prince Yi, Prince He, Grand Secretaries Ortai, Zhang Tingyu, and Xu Ben, and Ministers Neqin and Laibao to investigate. They were to demand which withheld memorial he meant had leaked, and whom among the powerful he accused of bribing the inner circle—when, he said, there was no inner circle to bribe and no magnate who could— and to answer directly.

sentences.zh: 鄂善僕及居間納賕者，皆承鄂善得俞氏賄，和親王等以聞。

translations.literal: E Shan's servants and the go-betweens who took bribes all admitted that E Shan had received bribes from the Yu family; Prince He and the others reported this.
translations.idiomatic: E Shan's servants and the middlemen who took bribes all confessed that E Shan had accepted Yu family money; Prince He and the others so reported.

sentences.zh: 上召和親王、鄂爾泰、訥親、來保同鄂善入見，上溫諭導其言，鄂善乃承得白金千。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Prince He, Ortai, Neqin, and Laibao together with E Shan for audience; the emperor gently guided his words, and E Shan then admitted receiving one thousand taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Prince He, Ortai, Neqin, and Laibao to confront E Shan; speaking gently, he drew out a confession that E Shan had taken a thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 上諭鄂善曰：「汝罪於律當絞。

translations.literal: The emperor said to E Shan: "By law your crime merits strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told E Shan: "By law you deserve strangulation.

sentences.zh: 汝嘗為大臣，不忍棄諸市。

translations.literal: You once served as a great minister; I cannot bear to abandon you in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: You were once a great minister; I cannot leave you to the execution ground.

sentences.zh: 然汝亦何顏復立於人世乎？

translations.literal: Yet how can you bear again to stand among men?
translations.idiomatic: Yet how can you face the world again?

sentences.zh: 汝宜有以自處。」

translations.literal: You should find some way to settle matters yourself."
translations.idiomatic: You must decide for yourself what to do."

sentences.zh: 既又下和親王等會大學士張廷玉、福敏、徐本，尚書海望，侍郎舒赫德詳議，如上諭。

translations.literal: Then he also ordered Prince He and the others to confer with Grand Secretaries Zhang Tingyu, Fu Min, and Xu Ben and Ministers Haiwang and Vice Minister Shuhede for detailed deliberation, as the emperor had instructed.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Prince He and the others to confer with Grand Secretaries Zhang Tingyu, Fu Min, and Xu Ben and Ministers Haiwang and Vice Minister Shuhede, as he had directed.

sentences.zh: 乃命訥親、來保持王大臣奏示鄂善，鄂善乃言未嘗受賕。

translations.literal: He then ordered Neqin and Laibao to present the memorial of the princes and ministers to E Shan, and E Shan then said he had never accepted bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Neqin and Laibao were told to show E Shan the princes' and ministers' report; E Shan then denied ever taking a bribe.

sentences.zh: 上因怒責鄂善欺罔，奪職下刑部，又命福敏、海望、舒赫德會鞫，論絞，上仍令賜死。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon angrily rebuked E Shan for deception, stripped him of office and handed him to the Ministry of Punishments, again ordered Fu Min, Haiwang, and Shuhede jointly to try the case, sentenced him to strangulation, and yet still ordered that he be granted death by imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor furiously accused E Shan of lying, stripped him and sent him to the Ministry of Punishments, had Fu Min, Haiwang, and Shuhede try him again, fixed strangulation—and still granted him suicide by imperial mercy.

sentences.zh: 家駒、浩並奪職。

translations.literal: Jiaju and Hao were also stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jiaju and Chen Hao were dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 永檀答上詢宣洩留中事，舉吳士功密劾史貽直以對。

translations.literal: When the emperor questioned Yongtan about the leaked secret memorial, he cited Wu Shigong's secret impeachment of Shi Yizhi in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Asked which secret memorial had leaked, Yongtan answered with Wu Shigong's secret impeachment of Shi Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 和親王等諮察大學士趙國麟等赴俞氏會喪雖無其事，然語有所自來。

translations.literal: Prince He and the others inquired and found that although Grand Secretary Zhao Guolin and others had not in fact attended the Yu family's mourning, yet the talk had some source.
translations.idiomatic: Prince He and the others found that Grand Secretary Zhao Guolin and others had not attended the Yu funeral, yet the rumor was not baseless.

sentences.zh: 上乃獎永檀摘姦發伏，直陳無隱，擢僉都御史。

translations.literal: The Emperor then commended Yongtan for exposing hidden wrongdoing and speaking frankly without concealment, and promoted him to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then praised Yongtan for uncovering hidden misconduct and speaking out without reserve, and promoted him to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 國麟獨奏辨，言：「永檀風聞言事，以蒙恩坐論之崇班，而被以跪拜細人之醜行。

translations.literal: Guo Guolin alone memorialized in defense, saying: 'Yongtan hears rumors and speaks on affairs; because he received grace he sits in exalted rank, yet is charged with the ugly conduct of a petty man who refuses to bow and kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Guolin alone submitted a rebuttal, saying: "Yongtan reports what he hears; he was raised to high rank as a reward, yet is now reproached for the petty offense of refusing to bow and kneel.

sentences.zh: 事有流弊，宜防其漸。

translations.literal: When affairs have a drifting evil, one should guard against its gradual growth.
translations.idiomatic: When a practice tends toward abuse, one should check it before it takes root.

sentences.zh: 數有往復，當保其終。

translations.literal: When there are repeated back-and-forth exchanges, one should preserve a good ending.
translations.idiomatic: When policy swings back and forth, one must see it through to a sound conclusion.

sentences.zh: 明季言路與政府各分門戶，互相擠排，綱紀浸以大壞。

translations.literal: In the late Ming the remonstrance channel and the government each formed its own faction and mutually squeezed and excluded, until discipline was greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming, the censorial remonstrance and the executive government each formed separate camps and mutually ostracized one another, until public order was deeply undermined.

sentences.zh: 在今日權無旁撓，言無偏聽，寧為未然之慮，不弛將至之防。

translations.literal: At present power has no rival interference, and words have no partial hearing; better to take precautions against what has not yet happened than to relax guard against what is about to come.
translations.idiomatic: Today no power rivals the throne, and no voice enjoys a partial ear; it is better to guard against evils not yet arisen than to slacken before dangers about to arrive.

sentences.zh: 乞特降諭旨，明示天下，以超擢永檀為獎其果敢，宥其冒昧。

translations.literal: I beg that a special edict be issued, made clear to all under Heaven, stating that Yongtan's extraordinary promotion rewards his boldness and pardons his presumption.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty issue a special edict, promulgated throughout the realm, explaining that Yongtan's rapid promotion rewards his courage while indulging his rashness.

sentences.zh: 嗣後凡詆斥大臣按之無實者，別有處分。

translations.literal: Henceforth, whenever anyone denounces a great minister and investigation finds no substance, there shall be separate punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whenever someone denounces a senior minister without substantiation, separate penalties shall apply.

sentences.zh: 則功過不相掩，而賞罰無偏曲。

translations.literal: Then merit and fault will not mask each other, and rewards and punishments will not be partial or crooked.
translations.idiomatic: Then merit and fault will not cancel each other out, and rewards and punishments will not be skewed.

sentences.zh: 如以臣言過戇，乞賜罷斥，或容解退，以全初心。」

translations.literal: If my words are overly blunt, I beg to be dismissed, or permitted to resign, so as to preserve my original intent.'
translations.idiomatic: If my words are too blunt, I beg dismissal, or leave to resign, that my original purpose may remain intact."

sentences.zh: 上手詔謂：「超擢永檀，亦善善欲長、惡惡欲短之意，大學士所云，老成遠慮，朕甚嘉納。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon issued an edict saying: 'The extraordinary promotion of Yongtan also embodies the intent to encourage good at length and cut short evil; what the Grand Secretary has said shows mature and far-sighted concern, which I greatly approve and accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then issued an edict: "Raising Yongtan so swiftly also reflects the wish to nurture good and curtail evil. The Grand Secretary's words show seasoned foresight, and I welcome them gladly.

sentences.zh: 其入閣視事，毋違朕意。」

translations.literal: Enter the Grand Secretariat and attend to affairs; do not go against my intent.'
translations.idiomatic: Take up your duties in the Grand Secretariat and do not depart from my intent."

sentences.zh: 而國麟求去益力，給事中盧秉純劾國麟，謂：「上詢國麟嘗會俞氏喪否，出以告其戚休致光祿寺卿劉籓長，語無狀。」

translations.literal: Yet Guo Guolin pressed his request to leave all the more forcefully; Supervising Censor Lu Bingchun impeached Guo Guolin, saying: "When the Emperor asked whether Guo Guolin had attended the Yu family's mourning, he went out and told this to his kinsman, the retired Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Liu Fanzhang, in improper terms."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Guolin pressed his resignation all the harder; Supervising Censor Lu Bingchun impeached him, alleging that "when the Emperor had asked whether Guo had attended the Yu family's mourning, Guo had left and told his kinsman Liu Fanzhang, a retired director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, in unseemly language."

sentences.zh: 上召籓長，令鄂爾泰、張廷玉、徐本、訥親、來保按其事，因謂籓長市井小人，國麟與論姻，又嘗奏薦，事非是。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Liu Fanzhang and ordered O-er-tai, Zhang Tingyu, Xu Ben, Neqin, and Laibao to investigate the matter, saying that Liu Fanzhang was a common market petty man, that Guo Guolin had discussed marriage with him and had once memorialized to recommend him—the affair was not right.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Liu Fanzhang and ordered O-er-tai, Zhang Tingyu, Xu Ben, Neqin, and Laibao to investigate, remarking that Liu was a vulgar man of the marketplace, that Guo had contemplated marriage ties with him and had once recommended him by memorial—the conduct was improper.

sentences.zh: 遣鄂爾泰等諭意，令請退。

translations.literal: He sent O-er-tai and the others to convey his intent and order Guo to request retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched O-er-tai and the others to convey his wishes and instruct Guo to seek retirement.

sentences.zh: 居數日，國麟疏不至，乃特詔左遷，留京師待缺。
