translations.literal: After several days Guo Guolin's memorial of retirement had not arrived; the Emperor then specially issued an edict his demotion by one rank, leaving him in the capital awaiting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When after several days Guo's retirement memorial still had not come, the Emperor specially ordered him demoted one rank and kept in the capital awaiting a new post.

sentences.zh: 秉純語過當，籓長刺探何緣被譴，不謹，皆奪職。

translations.literal: Lu Bingchun's words were excessive; Liu Fanzhang inquired how he came to be punished—imprudent conduct—and both were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bingchun had overreached in his language; Liu Fanzhang pried into why he had been punished—careless conduct—and both were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 又擢永檀左副都御史。

translations.literal: Yongtan was again promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yongtan was again promoted to left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 貴州甕安民羅尚珍詣都察院訴家居原任四川巡撫王士俊侵其墓地，命永檀如貴州會總督張廣泗按治，士俊論罪如律。

translations.literal: Luo Shangzhen, a commoner of Weng'an in Guizhou, came to the Censorate to complain that Wang Shijun, formerly Governor of Sichuan, in his home district had encroached on his family's grave land; the Emperor ordered Yongtan to go to Guizhou and jointly with Governor-General Zhang Guangsi investigate, and Wang Shijun was sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shangzhen, a commoner of Weng'an in Guizhou, petitioned the Censorate that Wang Shijun, formerly governor of Sichuan, had seized his family's burial ground at home; the Emperor ordered Yongtan to Guizhou to investigate jointly with Governor-General Zhang Guangsi, and Wang was convicted as the law required.

sentences.zh: 河南巡撫雅爾圖劾永檀自貴州還京師，道南陽，縱其僕撻村民，下部議罰俸。

translations.literal: Governor of Henan Ya'ertu impeached Yongtan, saying that on returning from Guizhou to the capital he passed through Nanyang and allowed his servants to beat village commoners; the ministry deliberated and fined his salary.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Governor Ya'ertu impeached Yongtan, charging that on his return from Guizhou he passed through Nanyang and let his servants beat villagers; the ministry deliberated and imposed a salary fine.

sentences.zh: 七年十二月，命如江南會巡撫週學健治賑，未行，永檀以密奏留中事告大學士鄂爾泰子鄂容安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventh year he was ordered to go to Jiangnan and jointly with Governor Zhou Xuejian manage relief; before he departed, Yongtan told O-er-tai's son O Rong'an about a secret memorial held back at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the seventh year he was ordered to Jiangnan to manage famine relief with Governor Zhou Xuejian; before setting out, Yongtan disclosed to Grand Secretary O-er-tai's son O Rong'an the matter of a secret memorial withheld at court.

sentences.zh: 上命奪職，下內務府慎刑司，令莊親王，履親王，和親王，平郡王，大學士張廷玉、徐本，尚書訥親、來保、哈達哈按其事。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered his dismissal from office and handed him to the Imperial Household Department's Office of Punishments; he ordered Prince Zhuang, Prince Lu, Prince He, Prince Ping, Grand Secretaries Zhang Tingyu and Xu Ben, and Ministers Neqin, Laibao, and Hadaha to investigate the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Yongtan stripped of office and remanded to the Imperial Household Department's Office of Punishments; he charged Prince Zhuang, Prince Lu, Prince He, Prince Ping, Grand Secretaries Zhang Tingyu and Xu Ben, and Ministers Neqin, Laibao, and Hadaha to try the case.

sentences.zh: 鄂容安、永檀自承未奏前商謀，既奏後照會。

translations.literal: O Rong'an and Yongtan themselves admitted that before the memorial was submitted they had consulted together, and after submission they exchanged notes.
translations.idiomatic: O Rong'an and Yongtan confessed that before the memorial was filed they had plotted together, and after filing they compared notes.

sentences.zh: 王大臣等用洩漏機密事務律論罪，上責其結黨營私，用律不合，令會三法司覆讞。

translations.literal: The princes and great ministers applied the statute on leaking confidential state affairs; the Emperor rebuked them for factional private dealing and said the statute did not fit, and ordered the Three Judicial Offices jointly to re-examine the case.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and senior ministers invoked the law on leaking state secrets; the Emperor rebuked them for forming cliques for private gain, declared the statute inapplicable, and ordered the Three Judicial Offices to review the verdict jointly.

sentences.zh: 王大臣等因請刑訊，並奪大學士鄂爾泰職逮問，上謂鄂爾泰受遺大臣，不忍深究，下吏議，示薄罰。

translations.literal: The princes and great ministers therefore requested judicial torture, and also sought to strip Grand Secretary O-er-tai of office and arrest him for questioning; the Emperor said O-er-tai had received the legacy of a great minister and he could not bear to probe deeply, and sent the matter to the officials for deliberation with a light penalty shown.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and ministers then asked for judicial torture and also sought to dismiss Grand Secretary O-er-tai and arrest him; the Emperor said O-er-tai stood in the succession of a great minister and he could not bring himself to pursue the matter deeply, and referred it to the officials for deliberation with a token penalty in view.

sentences.zh: 永檀、鄂容安亦不必刑訊，永檀受恩特擢，乃依附師門，有所論劾，無不豫先商酌，暗結黨援，排擠異己，罪重大；

translations.literal: Yongtan and O Rong'an also need not undergo judicial torture; Yongtan had received special grace in promotion, yet clung to his master's school—in every impeachment he had first consulted in secret, covertly forming factional support and squeezing out those unlike himself—the crime was grave;
translations.idiomatic: Yongtan and O Rong'an need not be tortured either; Yongtan had been specially favored with rapid promotion, yet attached himself to his patron's circle—for every accusation he had first plotted in secret, knitting factional ties and driving out dissent—the offense was serious;

sentences.zh: 鄂容安罪亦無可逭，但較永檀當末減。

translations.literal: O Rong'an's crime also could not be escaped, but compared with Yongtan he should receive the lesser penalty at the end.
translations.idiomatic: O Rong'an's guilt was likewise inescapable, but compared with Yongtan he deserved mitigation at sentencing.

sentences.zh: 命定擬具奏，奏未上，永檀卒於獄。

translations.literal: He ordered a fixed sentence to be prepared and memorialized; before the memorial was submitted, Yongtan died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a final sentence drafted and submitted; before the memorial reached him, Yongtan died in custody.

sentences.zh: 鄂容安論戍，上寬之，語在鄂容安傳。

translations.literal: O Rong'an was sentenced to banishment; the Emperor showed leniency—the account is in O Rong'an's biography.
translations.idiomatic: O Rong'an was sentenced to exile; the Emperor showed mercy—the details appear in his biography.

sentences.zh: 柴潮生，字禹門，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Chai Chaosheng, courtesy name Yumen, was a native of Renhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Chaosheng, whose courtesy name was Yumen, came from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年舉人，授內閣中書，充軍機處章京。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng he passed the provincial examination, was appointed Secretariat Drafting Clerk, and served as a clerk at the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongzheng he passed the provincial examination, was appointed a secretariat drafting clerk, and served as a clerk on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部主事。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，考選山西道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong he was selected by examination and appointed Supervising Censor of the Shanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qianlong he was chosen by examination and appointed supervising censor for the Shanxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 是歲旱，上降詔求言。

translations.literal: That year there was drought; the Emperor issued an edict seeking remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought drought; the Emperor issued an edict inviting candid counsel.

sentences.zh: 潮生疏言：「君諮臣儆，治世之休風；

translations.literal: Chaosheng memorialized, saying: 'The ruler consults ministers and ministers warn one another—this is the fine custom of an age of good government;
translations.idiomatic: Chaosheng submitted a memorial: "When the ruler seeks counsel and ministers admonish one another, that is the wholesome custom of a well-governed age;

sentences.zh: 益謙虧盈，檢身之至理。

translations.literal: to increase humility and reduce excess, and to examine oneself—this is the highest principle of self-discipline.
translations.idiomatic: to grow more humble and restrain excess, and to examine oneself—that is the supreme rule of personal discipline.

sentences.zh: 臣伏讀上諭有云：'爾九卿中能責難於君者何人？

translations.literal: Your subject has read reverently the imperial instruction that says, 'Among you Nine Ministers, who can reprove the ruler?
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has read with reverence the imperial words: "Among you nine ministers, who can hold the ruler to account?"

sentences.zh: 陳善閉邪者何事？

translations.literal: What affairs have you put forward to promote good and shut out evil?
translations.idiomatic: What have you done to advance good and bar evil?

sentences.zh: '此誠我皇上虛懷若谷、從諫弗咈之盛心也。

translations.literal: This is truly our Emperor's magnanimous heart, like a valley receiving all, that refuses to tire of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: This truly expresses our Emperor's open heart, deep as a valley, never weary of honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 今歲入春以來，近京雨澤未經霑足，宵旰焦勞，無時或釋。

translations.literal: From the spring of this year, near the capital rain has not fully reached the soil; Your Majesty toils day and night with anxiety, never finding release.
translations.idiomatic: Since spring this year the capital region has not received adequate rain; Your Majesty labors day and night in anxiety without respite.

sentences.zh: 惟是天時雨暘，難以窺測；

translations.literal: Heaven's timing of rain and sunshine is hard to fathom;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's gift of rain and sun is beyond prediction;

sentences.zh: 而人事修省，不妨過為責難。

translations.literal: yet human affairs of self-examination need not shrink from over-strict reproof.
translations.idiomatic: yet human effort at self-reform should not shy from the sternest self-criticism.

sentences.zh: 修省於事為者，一動一言，純雜易見；

translations.literal: Self-examination in visible conduct—in every move and word, purity or mixture is easily seen;
translations.idiomatic: Self-examination in outward conduct—in every act and word, what is pure or mixed is easily seen;

sentences.zh: 修省於隱微者，不聞不見，朕兆難窺。

translations.literal: self-examination in what is hidden—in what is neither heard nor seen, the first signs are hard to discern.
translations.idiomatic: self-examination in what is hidden—in what neither ear nor eye reaches, the first stirrings are hard to detect.

sentences.zh: 君心為萬化之源，普天率土，百司萬姓，皆於此託命焉。

translations.literal: The ruler's mind is the source of all transformation; all under Heaven and the myriad officials and people entrust their lives to it.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's mind is the fountain of all change; the empire and every office and subject stake their fate upon it.

sentences.zh: 皇上萬幾餘暇，豈無陶情適興之時？

translations.literal: When the Emperor has spare moments amid myriad affairs, are there not times to lift the mood and find diversion?
translations.idiomatic: Amid countless duties, does Your Majesty never have moments to refresh the spirit and take innocent pleasure?

sentences.zh: 但恐一念偶動，其端甚微，而自便自恕之機，或乘於不及覺，遂致潛滋暗長而莫可遏。

translations.literal: Yet I fear that when a thought moves by chance, the beginning is extremely slight, and the opportunity for self-indulgence and self-excuse may seize the moment before one is aware, until it secretly grows in the dark and cannot be checked.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear that when a single thought stirs by chance, the start is tiny, and the habit of indulgence and self-forgiveness may catch one unawares, until it spreads unseen and cannot be stopped.

sentences.zh: 則俄頃間之出入，即為皇功疏密所關。

translations.literal: Then the coming and going of a moment is what concerns whether imperial achievement is dense or loose.
translations.idiomatic: Then what passes through the mind in an instant bears on whether the imperial work is concentrated or diffuse.

sentences.zh: 伏乞皇上於百爾臣工所不及見，左右近習所不及窺，朝夕愈加劼毖，豈特隨時修省致感召之休徵已哉？」

translations.literal: I humbly beg the Emperor, in what the hundred officials cannot see and what those close at hand cannot peer into, to become daily more diligent and cautious—would this not do more than occasional self-examination to bring down blessings of harmonious response?'
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty, in what the whole bureaucracy cannot see and intimates cannot spy upon, to grow daily more vigilant and strict—would that not surpass sporadic self-examination in drawing down Heaven's favorable response?"

sentences.zh: 八年，天津、河間二府大旱。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the two prefectures of Tianjin and Hejian suffered great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the prefectures of Tianjin and Hejian suffered severe drought.

sentences.zh: 九年，潮生復疏言：「河間、天津二府經流之大河三：曰衛河，曰滹沱河，曰漳河。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Chaosheng again memorialized, saying: 'In the two prefectures of Hejian and Tianjin there are three great rivers that carry the flow: the Wei River, the Hutuo River, and the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Chaosheng memorialized again: "In Hejian and Tianjin the main rivers are three: the Wei, the Hutuo, and the Zhang.

sentences.zh: 其餘河間分水之支河十有一，瀦水之淀泊十有七，蓄水之渠三；

translations.literal: Besides these, in Hejian there are eleven branch rivers that divide the water, seventeen marsh lakes that hold water, and three channels that store water;
translations.idiomatic: Besides these, Hejian has eleven distributary streams, seventeen storage marshes, and three retention canals;

sentences.zh: 天津分水之支河十有三，瀦水之淀泊十有四，受水之沽六：水道至多。

translations.literal: in Tianjin there are thirteen branch rivers that divide the water, fourteen marsh lakes that hold water, and six outlets that receive water—the waterways are extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin has thirteen branch streams, fourteen storage marshes, and six receiving estuaries—the water network is vast.

sentences.zh: 向若河渠深廣，蓄洩有方，旱歲不能全收灌溉之功，亦可得半。

translations.literal: If formerly rivers and channels had been deep and wide and storage and discharge properly arranged, even in drought years the full benefit of irrigation could not be obtained, yet half could still be gained.
translations.idiomatic: Had the rivers and canals been kept deep and wide with storage and release properly managed, even in drought years full irrigation could not always be achieved, yet half the benefit might still be secured.

sentences.zh: 即不然，而平日之蓄積，亦可支持數月，以需大澤之至。

translations.literal: If not so, the accumulation of ordinary days could still support several months, awaiting the arrival of great soaking rains.
translations.idiomatic: Even otherwise, water stored in normal times could sustain the land for months, until heavy rains arrived.

sentences.zh: 何至拋田棄宅，挈子攜妻，流離道路哉？

translations.literal: How could it come to abandoning fields and dwellings, taking children and wives, and wandering destitute on the roads?
translations.idiomatic: How then could people abandon fields and homes, take up children and wives, and flee starving along the roads?

sentences.zh: 水利之廢，即此可知矣。

translations.literal: The ruin of water conservancy can be known from this.
translations.idiomatic: The collapse of water management is plain from this.

sentences.zh: 甘霖一日不足，則賑費固不可已。

translations.literal: One day of sweet rain insufficient, then relief expenses indeed cannot cease.
translations.idiomatic: When even one day of good rain fails, relief spending cannot stop.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為徒費之於賑恤，不如大發帑金，遴遣大臣經理畿輔水利，俾以濟饑民、消旱潦，且轉貧乏之區為富饒。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that to spend in vain on relief and succor is inferior to releasing a large sum from the treasury and selecting great ministers to manage water conservancy in the capital region, thereby relieving famine victims, moderating flood and drought, and turning poor regions into rich ones.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes that pouring money into relief alone is inferior to releasing a large treasury sum and dispatching senior ministers to oversee water works in the capital region—feeding the hungry, easing drought and flood, and turning poor districts prosperous.

sentences.zh: 救時之急務，籌國之遠謨，莫以易此。

translations.literal: For urgent rescue of the time and far-reaching planning for the state, nothing equals this.
translations.idiomatic: For immediate crisis and long-term national planning, nothing surpasses this.

sentences.zh: 臣考漢張堪為漁陽太守，於狐奴開稻田八千頃，狐奴今"昌平也。

translations.literal: Your subject examines Han Zhang Kan as Administrator of Yuyang, who opened eight thousand qing of paddy at Hunu—Hunu is present-day Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject cites Han Zhang Kan, who as administrator of Yuyang opened eight thousand qing of rice fields at Hunu—today's Changping.

sentences.zh: 北齊裴延俊為幽州刺史，修古督亢坡，溉田萬餘畝，督亢今涿州也。

translations.literal: Northern Qi Pei Yanjun as Regional Inspector of Youzhou restored the ancient Dukang Slope and irrigated more than ten thousand mu—Dukang is present-day Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Qi, Pei Yanjun as regional inspector of Youzhou restored the ancient Dukang Slope and irrigated more than ten thousand mu—Dukang is today's Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 宋何承矩為河北制置使，於雄、鄚、霸州興堰六百里灌田。

translations.literal: Song He Chengju as Commissioner for Hebei built dikes six hundred li long to irrigate fields in Xiong, Mo, and Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Song, He Chengju as Hebei commissioner built dikes six hundred li long to irrigate land in Xiong, Mo, and Ba.

sentences.zh: 明汪應蛟為天津巡撫，捐俸開二千畝，畝收四五石。

translations.literal: Ming Wang Yingjiao as Governor of Tianjin donated his salary and opened two thousand mu, each mu yielding four or five shi.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming, Wang Yingjiao as Tianjin governor contributed his salary and opened two thousand mu yielding four or five shi per mu.

sentences.zh: 今東西二淀，即承矩之塘濼，天津十字圍，即應蛟水田之遺址。

translations.literal: Today's eastern and western marshes are He Chengju's Tangluo; Tianjin's Shiziwei is the site of Wang Yingjiao's paddy fields.
translations.idiomatic: Today's eastern and western storage marshes are He Chengju's Tangluo; Tianjin's Shiziwei is where Wang Yingjiao's paddies stood.

sentences.zh: 國朝李光地為巡撫，請興河間水田，言涿州水占之地，每畝售錢二百，開成水田畝易銀十兩。

translations.literal: In our dynasty Li Guangdi as governor requested development of Hejian paddy, saying that land occupied by Zhuozhou's waters sold for two hundred cash per mu, but once opened as paddy each mu could exchange for ten taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty Governor Li Guangdi asked to develop Hejian paddies, noting that flooded Zhuozhou land sold for two hundred cash per mu, yet once converted to paddy fetched ten taels of silver per mu.

sentences.zh: 上年總督高斌請開永定河灌田，亦云查勘所至，眾情欣悅。

translations.literal: Last year Governor-General Gao Bin requested opening the Yongding River for irrigation, likewise saying that wherever survey reached, the people rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Governor-General Gao Bin proposed irrigating from the Yongding River, likewise reporting universal joy wherever surveys went.

sentences.zh: 臣聞石景山有莊頭修姓，自引渾河灌田，比常農畝收數倍。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that at Shijingshan an estate steward surnamed Xiu drew the Hun River to irrigate fields and harvested several times the usual yield per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that at Shijingshan an estate steward named Xiu diverted the Hun River to irrigate and reaped several times the normal harvest per mu.

sentences.zh: 蠡縣亦有富戶自行鑿井，旱歲能收其利。

translations.literal: In Li County a wealthy household also dug wells on its own and in drought years could still profit.
translations.idiomatic: In Li County a rich household dug its own wells and profited even in drought years.

sentences.zh: 霸州知州硃一蜚勸民開井二十餘口，民頗賴之。

translations.literal: Bazhou Prefect Zhu Yifei urged the people to open more than twenty wells, on which they relied heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Bazhou Prefect Zhu Yifei persuaded the people to sink more than twenty wells, which they came to depend on.

sentences.zh: 證之近事，复確有據，則水利之可興也決矣。

translations.literal: Verified by recent events, there is again solid evidence—then the feasibility of developing water conservancy is decided.
translations.idiomatic: Recent examples furnish solid proof—water development can surely succeed.

sentences.zh: 今請特遣大臣齎帑金數十萬兩，往河間、天津二府，督同道府牧令，分委佐貳雜職，除運道所關，及滹沱正流水性暴急，慎勿輕動，其餘河渠淀泊，凡有故跡可尋者，皆重加疏浚。

translations.literal: Your subject now asks that a great minister specially be sent bearing several hundred thousand taels of treasury silver to the two prefectures of Hejian and Tianjin, supervising together with circuit intendants, prefects, and magistrates, delegating to assistant and miscellaneous officials; except for routes vital to transport and the main current of the Hutuo whose nature is violently swift—take care not to disturb them lightly—all other rivers, channels, and marshes where old traces can be traced should be heavily dredged anew.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject asks that a senior minister be sent with several hundred thousand taels to Hejian and Tianjin to supervise circuit, prefectural, and county officials and their deputies; save transport arteries and the violent main stream of the Hutuo, which must not be lightly tampered with, every river, canal, and marsh with recoverable traces should be thoroughly dredged.

sentences.zh: 又於河渠淀泊之旁，各開小河；

translations.literal: Also beside rivers, channels, and marshes, open small streams on each side;
translations.idiomatic: Beside each river, canal, and marsh, open smaller streams;

sentences.zh: 小河之旁，各開大溝：皆務深廣，度水力不及則止。

translations.literal: beside small streams, open large ditches—all to be made as deep and wide as possible, stopping where water power cannot reach.
translations.idiomatic: beside those streams, open main ditches—all as deep and wide as feasible, stopping where the water cannot carry.

sentences.zh: 節次建立水門，遞相灌注。

translations.literal: Establish sluice gates in sequence for mutual irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: Build sluice gates in stages to feed one another.

sentences.zh: 旱則引水入溝以溉田，潦則放閘歸河以洩水。

translations.literal: In drought, lead water into ditches to irrigate fields; in flood, open gates to return water to rivers and discharge it.
translations.idiomatic: In drought, channel water into ditches for irrigation; in flood, open the gates and send water back to the rivers.

sentences.zh: 其離水遼遠之處，每田一頃，掘井一口，十頃掘大塘一口，亦足供用。

translations.literal: Where land lies far from water, for each qing of field dig one well; for each ten qing dig one large pond—also sufficient for use.
translations.idiomatic: Where fields stand far from water, sink one well per qing and one large pond per ten qing—enough for practical use.

sentences.zh: 其中有侵及民田，並古陂廢堰為民業已久者，皆計畝均分撥還，即將​​現在受賑饑民及外來流民，停其賑給，按地分段，就工給值，酌予口糧，寧厚無減。

translations.literal: Where private fields are encroached upon, and ancient dykes and abandoned weirs long become people's livelihoods, all should be calculated by mu and evenly divided and returned; then stop relief to famine victims presently receiving aid and incoming refugees, assign them by land in sections, pay wages for labor, and grant rations in measured amounts—better generous than reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Where works encroach on private land or ancient dykes long turned to livelihood, compensate by mu and restore shares; then suspend grain relief to current famine victims and refugees, assign them by section to paid labor, and grant rations generously rather than stingily.

sentences.zh: 一人在役，停其家賑糧二口；

translations.literal: One person in service—suspend relief grain for two persons in his household;
translations.idiomatic: One family member on the works—suspend relief for two mouths at home;

sentences.zh: 二人在役，停其家賑糧四口。

translations.literal: two persons in service—suspend relief grain for four persons in the household.
translations.idiomatic: Two on the works—suspend relief for four at home.

sentences.zh: 其餘口及一戶皆不能執役者，仍如例給賑。

translations.literal: The remaining mouths and households where none can labor shall still receive relief as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining dependents and households unable to work should still receive relief as before.

sentences.zh: 其疏濬之處，有可耕種，即藉予工本，分年徵還。

translations.literal: Where dredging opens land fit for planting, lend capital for planting and collect repayment over years.
translations.idiomatic: Where dredging yields cultivable land, lend seed and tools and recover the cost over successive years.

sentences.zh: 更請別簡大臣，齎帑金分巡直隸各府，一如河間、天津二府，次第舉行。

translations.literal: Your subject further asks that another great minister be selected bearing treasury silver to tour each prefecture of Zhili, proceeding in order just as in the two prefectures of Hejian and Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject further asks that another minister be chosen with treasury funds to tour every Zhili prefecture in the same phased manner as Hejian and Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 或曰：'北土高燥，不宜稻種，土性沙鹼，水入即滲，挖掘民地，易起怨聲。

translations.literal: Some say: 'Northern soil is high and dry, unsuited to rice; the soil is sandy and saline, and water sinks in at once; digging up people's land easily raises complaints.'
translations.idiomatic: Objectors say: "Northern ground is high and dry, ill suited to rice; soil is sandy and salty and water sinks away; digging up private land provokes resentment."

sentences.zh: 前朝徐貞明行之而立敗，怡賢親王與大學士硃軾之經理亦垂成而坐廢，可為明鑑。

translations.literal: Formerly Xu Zhenming of the previous dynasty tried it and failed at once; Prince Yi Xian and Grand Secretary Zhu Shi managed it and, on the verge of success, abandoned it—clear warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhenming in the previous dynasty tried and failed immediately; Prince Yi Xian and Grand Secretary Zhu Shi nearly succeeded yet abandoned the work—a plain warning.

sentences.zh: '臣按九土之種異宜，未聞稻非冀州之產，玉田、豐潤秔稻油油。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that the nine soils each have different suitability; I have never heard that rice is not a product of Jizhou—Yutian and Fengrun glutinous rice grows lush.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject notes that soils differ in what they bear; rice is not unknown in Jizhou—Yutian and Fengrun produce fine japonica in abundance.

sentences.zh: 且今第為之興水利耳，固不必強之為水田也。

translations.literal: Moreover, what is sought now is merely to develop water conservancy; there is no need to force paddy fields.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the proposal is only to restore water works; no one need force paddies.

sentences.zh: 或疏或浚，則用官資，可稻可禾，聽從民便。

translations.literal: Whether dredging or digging, use official funds; rice or grain crops—follow the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Whether dredging or digging, spend public money; plant rice or dry grain as the people prefer.

sentences.zh: 此不疑者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first point without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first objection answered.

sentences.zh: 土性沙鹼，是誠有之，不過數處耳，豈遍地皆沙鹼乎？

translations.literal: Sandy saline soil indeed exists, but only in a few places—are they sandy and saline everywhere?
translations.idiomatic: Sandy, salty soil exists, but only here and there—is the whole region nothing but sand and salt?

sentences.zh: 且即使沙鹼，而多一行水之道，比聽其衝溢者不猶愈於已乎？

translations.literal: And even if sandy and saline, is one more channel for water not still better than letting floods spill unchecked?
translations.idiomatic: Even where soil is sandy and salty, an extra watercourse still beats unchecked overflow.

sentences.zh: 此不疑者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second point without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second objection answered.

sentences.zh: 若以溝渠為捐地，尤非知農事者。

translations.literal: If one treats ditches and canals as donated land, that is especially not to know farming affairs.
translations.idiomatic: To treat canal land as pure loss shows ignorance of farming.

sentences.zh: 凡力田者，務盡力而不貴多墾。

translations.literal: Those who work fields strive to use their strength fully and do not prize excessive opening of land.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers exhaust their strength on what they till and do not crave ever more acreage.

sentences.zh: 今使十畝之地，捐一畝以蓄水，而九畝倍收，較十畝皆薄入孰利？

translations.literal: If on ten mu of land one mu is donated to hold water and the other nine mu double their harvest, compared with ten mu all yielding thin crops—which is more profitable?
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice one mu of ten to store water and the other nine may double their yield—is that not better than ten mu of meager harvest?

sentences.zh: 況捐者又予撥還。

translations.literal: Moreover, what is donated is also calculated and returned by division.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, donated land is compensated and restored by measure.

sentences.zh: 此不疑者三也。

translations.literal: This is the third point without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third objection answered.

sentences.zh: 至前人屢行屢罷，此亦有由，貞明所言百世之利，其時御史王之棟參劾，出於奄人勳戚之意。

translations.literal: As for predecessors who tried repeatedly and stopped repeatedly, there are reasons: what Xu Zhenming called benefit for a hundred generations—in his day Supervising Censor Wang Zhidong impeached him, out of the intent of eunuchs and meritorious kin.
translations.idiomatic: As for earlier efforts that started and stopped, there were causes: Xu Zhenming spoke of benefit for a hundred generations, yet Supervising Censor Wang Zhidong impeached him at the instigation of eunuchs and imperial in-laws.

sentences.zh: 其疏亦第言滹沱不可開，未嘗言水田不可行也。

translations.literal: His memorial also only said the Hutuo could not be opened—it never said paddy fields could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial said only that the Hutuo should not be opened—it never said paddies could not be tried.

sentences.zh: 但其募南人開墾​​，即以地予之，又許佔籍。

translations.literal: But when recruiting southerners to open wasteland, they gave them the land outright and also permitted local registration.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recruiting southerners to reclaim land they granted them the plots outright and even allowed them to register locally for the examinations.

sentences.zh: 左光斗之屯學亦然。

translations.literal: Zuo Guangdou's military-colony schools were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Guangdou's colony-and-school schemes worked the same way.

sentences.zh: 是奪北人之田，又塞其功名之路，其致人言也宜矣。

translations.literal: This seized northerners' fields and also blocked their path to rank through the examinations—it was fitting that it drew talk.
translations.idiomatic: They took land from northerners and shut them out of the examination ladder; no wonder it provoked widespread complaint.

sentences.zh: 至營田四局，成績具在。

translations.literal: As for the four Bureaus of Garrison Farming, their achievements are fully on record.
translations.idiomatic: The record of the four garrison-farming bureaus speaks for itself.

sentences.zh: 當日效力差員，不無舉行未善，所以賢王一沒，遂過而廢之，非深識長算者之所出也。

translations.literal: The staff who served then were not without faults in execution; yet when the worthy prince died they were faulted and the work abandoned—that is not what men of deep insight and long calculation would counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Some agents back then performed poorly, yet when the worthy prince died the whole project was condemned and scrapped—hardly the counsel of statesmen who think in generations.

sentences.zh: 非常之原，黎民所懼，所貴持久，乃可有功。

translations.literal: At the outset extraordinary undertakings frighten the common people; what is prized is endurance—only then can there be achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Bold ventures at first alarm the people; only persistence turns them into lasting success.

sentences.zh: 秦開鄭、白之渠，利及百世，而當時至欲殺水工鄭國。

translations.literal: Qin opened the Zheng and Bai canals and the benefit lasted a hundred generations, yet at the time they even wanted to kill the waterworks engineer Zheng Guo.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin dug the Zheng and Bai canals the gain endured for centuries, yet at the time the court nearly executed the engineer Zheng Guo.

sentences.zh: 漢河東太守番系引汾水灌田，河渠數徙，田者不能償種。

translations.literal: In Han, Fan Xi, governor of Hedong, led Fen River water to irrigate fields; the channels shifted repeatedly and farmers could not recover even their seed grain.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han, Hedong governor Fan Xi drew the Fen to irrigate fields, but as the channels kept shifting farmers could not recoup their seed.

sentences.zh: 至唐長孫恕复鑿之，畝收十石。

translations.literal: By Tang, Changsun Shu reopened it, and the yield per mu reached ten shi.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang, Changsun Shu reopened the works and harvests reached ten shi per mu.

sentences.zh: 凡始事難，成事易。

translations.literal: In all matters, beginning is hard and completing is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Every great work is hard to start and easy to finish once it is underway.

sentences.zh: 賡續以終之則是，中道而棄之則非。

translations.literal: To continue and carry it through is right; to abandon it halfway is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: To see it through is right; to quit midway is wrong.

sentences.zh: 此不疑者四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth point on which there should be no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth matter beyond reasonable doubt.

sentences.zh: 至水利既興，招募農師，造作水器，逐年作何經理，俾永無湮塞，應聽在事大臣詳加籌畫。

translations.literal: Once waterworks are established, recruit farming masters, make water tools, and plan year-by-year management so they never silt shut—the ministers in charge should be heard in detailed planning.
translations.idiomatic: Once irrigation is in place, recruit skilled farmers, build sluices and tools, and lay out yearly upkeep so channels never choke up—let the responsible ministers plan this in detail.

sentences.zh: 皇上視民如子，凡有賑恤，千萬帑金亦無可惜。

translations.literal: The Emperor regards the people as his children; whenever there is relief and succor, even tens of millions from the treasury is not begrudged.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty treats the people as his children; for relief and succor, even ten million taels from the treasury would not be too much.

sentences.zh: 即如開通京師溝道，估費二十餘萬，以視興修一省水利，輕重較然。

translations.literal: Even opening the capital's drainage ditches was estimated at more than two hundred thousand—compared with developing a whole province's waterworks, the relative weight is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Clearing the capital's drainage alone was estimated at over two hundred thousand taels—against reviving an entire province's hydraulics, the relative cost is plain.

sentences.zh: 況此舉乃以阜財，非以費財。

translations.literal: Moreover this measure is to enrich revenue, not merely to spend it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover this project builds wealth; it is not mere expenditure.

sentences.zh: 天災國家代有，荒政未有百全，何如擲百萬於水濱，而立收國富民安之效？

translations.literal: Heaven's disasters visit every dynasty; famine policy is never perfectly sure—why not commit a million at the water's edge and at once reap a rich state and settled people?
translations.idiomatic: Natural calamities repeat in every age, and famine relief is never foolproof—why not invest a million on river works and promptly secure a rich state and contented people?

sentences.zh: 縱有堯災湯旱，亦可挹彼注茲，是謂無弊之賑恤。

translations.literal: Even were there Yao's floods or Tang's droughts, one could draw from that to pour into this—this is relief without drawback.
translations.idiomatic: Even Yao's floods or Tang's droughts could be met by shifting water from abundance to want—relief without lasting harm.

sentences.zh: 連年米價屢廑聖懷，盡停採買，豈可久行？

translations.literal: In recent years grain prices have repeatedly weighed on the sacred mind; to halt government purchase entirely—can that be sustained long?
translations.idiomatic: Grain prices have weighed on Your Majesty year after year; suspending government purchases entirely cannot be sustained forever.

sentences.zh: 捐監輸倉，亦非上策。

translations.literal: Donations for student status to fill granaries is also not the best policy.
translations.idiomatic: Selling the student quota to fill the granaries is no superior solution either.

sentences.zh: 若小民收穫素裕，自然二鬴有資。

translations.literal: If common people were always ample in harvest, naturally they would have means for two meals.
translations.idiomatic: If ordinary farmers were steadily well-off at harvest, they would naturally afford two meals a day.

sentences.zh: 臣訪問直隸士民，皆云：『有水之田較無水之田，相去不啻再倍。』

translations.literal: Your subject inquired among gentry and commoners of Zhili; all said: "Fields with water compared with fields without water differ by no less than double."
translations.idiomatic: I questioned officials and commoners in Zhili; all said, "Irrigated land yields more than twice what dry land does."

sentences.zh: 是謂不竭之常平。

translations.literal: This is an ever-normal granary that never runs dry.
translations.idiomatic: This is an ever-normal granary that never runs empty.

sentences.zh: 近畿多八旗莊地，直隸亦京兆股肱，皆宜致之富饒，始可居重馭輕。

translations.literal: Near the capital there are many Eight Banner estate lands; Zhili too is the capital region's vital limb—all should be brought to abundance so one may hold the heavy and control the light.
translations.idiomatic: The capital environs hold many Banner estates; Zhili is the metropolis's vital province—both should be made prosperous so the center can anchor the realm.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝徙豪民於關中，明成祖遷富家於帝里，固非王政，不失深謀。

translations.literal: Han Wudi moved powerful families to Guanzhong; Ming Chengzu moved wealthy households to the imperial capital—though not orthodox kingship, the stratagem was shrewd.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi resettled great clans in Guanzhong and Ming Chengzu moved rich families to the capital—harsh perhaps, but far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 若水利既興，自然軍民兩利，是謂無形之帑藏。

translations.literal: If waterworks thrive, naturally both army and people benefit—this is a treasury without visible coffers.
translations.idiomatic: With irrigation thriving, army and people both gain—a treasury no vault can hold.

sentences.zh: 且雨者水土之氣所上騰而下澤也，土氣太甚，則水氣受制。

translations.literal: Moreover rain is the ascent of earth-and-water vapor and its descent to soak the land; when earth's vapor is too strong, water's vapor is constrained.
translations.idiomatic: Rain rises when earth and water breathe upward and falls when they soak the soil; when earth dominates, moisture is stifled.

sentences.zh: 直隸近年以來，閔雨者屢矣。

translations.literal: In Zhili in recent years prayers for rain have been repeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili has seen repeated drought prayers in recent years.

sentences.zh: 但使水土均調，自可雨暘時若，是謂有驗之調燮。

translations.literal: Only let earth and water balance and timely rain and sunshine will follow—this is harmonizing with proof of effect.
translations.idiomatic: Balance earth and water and seasonable rain and sun follow—proved harmony with nature.

sentences.zh: 且水性分之則利，合之則害；

translations.literal: Moreover water's nature: divided it benefits, combined it harms;
translations.idiomatic: Water helps when channeled apart and harms when left to mass together;

sentences.zh: 用之則利，棄之則害。

translations.literal: used it benefits, abandoned it harms.
translations.idiomatic: used it profits, discarded it destroys.

sentences.zh: 故周用有言：『人人皆治田之人，即人人皆治水之人。』

translations.literal: Thus Zhou Yong said: "Everyone who tends fields is everyone who tends water."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yong said, "Whoever farms the land also governs the water."

sentences.zh: 張伯行亦主此論。

translations.literal: Zhang Boxxing also held this view.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Boxxing held the same view.

sentences.zh: 陸隴其為靈壽令，督民濬衛河。

translations.literal: Lu Longqi, as magistrate of Lingshou, supervised the people in dredging the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Lingshou, Lu Longqi pressed the people to dredge the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 其始頗有怨言，謂開無水之河以病民；

translations.literal: At first there was much complaint, saying they were opening a waterless river to harm the people;
translations.idiomatic: At first there was grumbling that he was digging a dry riverbed to burden the people;

sentences.zh: 既而水潦大至，獨靈壽有宣導，歲竟有秋。

translations.literal: Then great floods came; Lingshou alone had channels to guide the water, and at year's end there was harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Then floods struck; only Lingshou had channels to carry them off, and that year ended in harvest.

sentences.zh: 貨殖者旱則資舟，為國者備斯無患，是謂隱寓之河防。

translations.literal: Merchants in drought rely on boats; for the state to prepare thus is to be without worry—this is hidden river defense.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants turn to boats in drought; a state that prepares so need not fear flood—implicit river control.

sentences.zh: 今生齒日繁，民食漸絀。

translations.literal: Now population grows daily and people's food gradually falls short.
translations.idiomatic: Population swells while the food supply thins.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為盡興西北之水田，闢東南之荒地，則米價自然平減。

translations.literal: Your subject foolishly holds that fully developing paddies in the northwest and opening wasteland in the southeast would naturally level and reduce grain prices.
translations.idiomatic: I believe developing paddies in the northwest and opening land in the southeast would naturally ease grain prices.

sentences.zh: 但事體至大，請先以直隸為端，行之有效，次第舉行。

translations.literal: But the matter is very great; please begin with Zhili as the start, and when it proves effective proceed step by step.
translations.idiomatic: The scheme is vast; begin in Zhili, and if it succeeds extend it gradually.

sentences.zh: 樂利萬年，庶其在此！」

translations.literal: Joy and benefit for ten thousand years—perhaps it lies here!"
translations.idiomatic: Lasting prosperity for ages may begin here!"

sentences.zh: 十年，疏陳理財三策，言：「治天下要務，惟用人、理財兩大事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he memorialized three policies for managing finances, saying: "The great tasks of ordering the realm are only two: employing men and managing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he submitted a memorial outlining three fiscal policies, saying: "Governing the empire turns on two great matters: appointing the right men and managing the treasury.

sentences.zh: 承平日久，供億浩繁，損上益下，日廑宸衷；

translations.literal: Long peace has lasted; supplies and expenditure are vast; harming the above to benefit the below daily weighs on the imperial heart;
translations.idiomatic: After long peace, state consumption has swelled; easing burdens on the people while revenue falters weighs on Your Majesty daily;

sentences.zh: 而量入為出，似尚未籌至計。

translations.literal: yet measuring income to match outlay seems not yet to have reached a thorough plan.
translations.idiomatic: yet matching expenditure to income still lacks a comprehensive plan.

sentences.zh: 禮曰：'財用足故百志成。

translations.literal: The Rites says: "When funds are sufficient, a hundred tasks succeed."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says, "When revenue is ample, a hundred undertakings succeed."

sentences.zh: '若少有窘乏，則蠲徵平賦、卹災厚下之大政俱不得施。

translations.literal: If there is even slight shortage, then the great policies of remitting levies, balancing taxes, relieving disasters, and enriching those below cannot all be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When funds run short, remissions, balanced taxation, disaster relief, and care for the poor—all the great policies of benevolent rule—cannot be fully applied.

sentences.zh: 遲之又久，則一切苟且之法隨之以起。

translations.literal: Delay it again and again and every expedient makeshift method will follow in its wake.
translations.idiomatic: Procrastinate long enough and stopgap expedients multiply.

sentences.zh: 此非天下之小故也。

translations.literal: This is no small matter for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: This is no minor concern for the empire.

sentences.zh: 頃見台臣請定會計疏，言每年所入三千六百萬，出亦三千六百萬。

translations.literal: Recently your subject saw a censorial memorial requesting fixed accounts, stating that annual income is thirty-six million and outgo likewise thirty-six million.
translations.idiomatic: Recently a censorial memorial proposed fixed accounts, stating annual revenue at thirty-six million taels and expenditure the same.

sentences.zh: 就今日計之，所入僅供所出。

translations.literal: Counting for today, income barely meets outgo.
translations.idiomatic: Measured for the present, revenue barely covers spending.

sentences.zh: 就異日計之，所入殆不足供所出。

translations.literal: Counting for days to come, income will scarcely suffice for outgo.
translations.idiomatic: Projected forward, revenue will likely fall short of need.

sentences.zh: 以皇上之仁明，國家之閒暇，而不籌一開源節流之法，為萬世無弊之方，是為失時。

translations.literal: With the Emperor's benevolence and clarity and the state's leisure, yet not devising a method to open sources and trim flow—a plan without flaw for ten thousand generations—is to miss the time.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's wisdom and the realm at peace, failure to devise lasting ways to increase revenue and cut waste is to miss the moment.

sentences.zh: 臣等荷恩，備官台省，不能少竭涓埃，協贊遠謨，是為負國。

translations.literal: We who have received grace and serve in the censorate and provincial offices cannot offer even a mote of effort to assist far-reaching design—that is to fail the state.
translations.idiomatic: We who serve in the censorate and provincial offices, though favored by grace, cannot contribute our mite to long-range planning—we fail the state.

sentences.zh: 以臣之計，一曰開邊外之屯田以養閒散，一曰給數年之俸餉散遣漢軍，一曰改捐監之款項以充公費，三者行而後良法美意可得而舉也。

translations.literal: By your subject's reckoning: first, open garrison farms beyond the frontier to support idle banner population; second, grant several years' pay and disperse the Han Banners; third, redirect purchase-for-student funds to public expenses—when these three are enacted, then good laws and fine intentions can be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In my view the remedies are three: open frontier garrison farms for idle bannermen; pay out several years' stipends and release the Han Banners; redirect student-purchase fees to provincial public funds. Only then can sound policies be implemented.

sentences.zh: 滿洲、蒙古、漢軍各有八旗，丁口蕃昌，視順治時蓋一衍為十，而生計艱難，視康熙時已十不及五，而且仰給於官而不已。

translations.literal: Manchu, Mongol, and Han each have Eight Banners; registered mouths flourish—compared with the Shunzhi era one has become ten in growth, yet livelihood is hard—compared with the Kangxi era not even five in ten—and still they rely on official support without end.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banners alike have seen registered population multiply tenfold since Shunzhi, while livelihoods are harder than in Kangxi—perhaps half as secure—and still they depend endlessly on state pay.

sentences.zh: 局於五百里之內而不使出，則將來上之弊必如北宋之養兵，下之弊亦必如有明之宗室，此不可不籌通變者也。

translations.literal: Confine them within five hundred li and not let them out, and in time the evil above will surely be like the Northern Song's keeping soldiers, and the evil below will surely be like the Ming imperial clans—this cannot go unaddressed with flexible reform.
translations.idiomatic: Pen them within five hundred li and the upper evil will mirror the Northern Song's burden of idle troops, the lower evil the Ming's ruinous imperial clans—this demands flexible reform.

sentences.zh: 臣聞奉天沿邊諸地，水泉肥美，請遣幹略大臣，分道經理。

translations.literal: Your subject hears that along the borders of Fengtian the springs and soil are rich and fine; please dispatch capable grand ministers to manage the routes separately.
translations.idiomatic: I am told the Fengtian frontier offers rich soil and good water; dispatch able ministers to develop it by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 視可屯之處，發帑建堡墩，起屋廬，置耕牛農具，令各旗滿洲除正身披甲在京當差，其次丁、餘丁力能耕者前往居住。

translations.literal: Where land can be garrison-farmed, disburse treasury funds to build forts and beacon towers, erect houses, provide plow oxen and farm tools, and order each Banner Manchu—aside from the primary register who wear armor and serve duty in the capital—to send secondary sons and surplus men able to farm to go and dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Where land can be farmed, spend treasury funds on forts, beacons, dwellings, oxen, and tools; let each Manchu Banner send secondary and surplus men able to farm, while primary registers remain armored on capital duty.

sentences.zh: 所耕之田，即付為永業，分年扣完工本，更不昇科。

translations.literal: The fields they till shall be granted as perpetual property; the cost of works shall be deducted over years and no further land tax shall be added.
translations.idiomatic: Grant tilled land as permanent holdings; recover construction costs over time without adding land tax.

sentences.zh: 惟令農隙操演，數年之後皆成勁卒。

translations.literal: Only order them to drill in farming intervals; after several years all will become crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: Require drill in farming slack seasons; in a few years they will become seasoned soldiers.

sentences.zh: 逐年發往軍台之人，令其分地捐貲效力，此後有原往者，令其陸續前往。

translations.literal: Each year send men to the military courier stations and have them contribute land and funds for service; thereafter those who wish to go may continue to go in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Each year assign men from the courier stations to contribute land and funds; thereafter volunteers may follow in turn.

sentences.zh: 此安頓滿洲閒散之法也。

translations.literal: This is the method for settling idle Manchu bannermen.
translations.idiomatic: This is how to settle idle Manchu banner population.

sentences.zh: 漢軍八旗已奉聽其出旗之旨，以定例太拘，故散遣寥寥。

translations.literal: The Han Eight Banners have already received the edict permitting them to leave the banners, but because the fixed regulations are too rigid, dispersal has been sparse.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Banners were already permitted to leave the banners, but rigid regulations have made release rare.

sentences.zh: 今請不論出仕與否，概許出旗。

translations.literal: Now please regardless of office-holding permit all to leave the banners.
translations.idiomatic: Now permit all to leave the banners whether or not they hold office.

sentences.zh: 其家現任居官者給三年俸餉，無居官者給六年俸餉。

translations.literal: Families with members currently in office shall receive three years' pay; those without officeholders shall receive six years' pay.
translations.idiomatic: Families with an incumbent official receive three years' stipend; others receive six.

sentences.zh: 其家產許之隨帶，任其自便。

translations.literal: Their household property may be taken along and they may go as they please.
translations.idiomatic: They may take their property and go where they will.

sentences.zh: 則貧富各不失所，而五年以後國帑節省無窮。

translations.literal: Then rich and poor each keep their place, and after five years the state treasury saves without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Rich and poor alike will find their footing, and after five years treasury savings will be immense.

sentences.zh: 即一時不能盡給，分作數年以次散遣，都統以下、章京以上各官，改補綠旗提鎮將弁。

translations.literal: Even if payment cannot be made all at once, disperse over several years in order; officials from commanders-in-chief down to clerks above a certain rank shall be reassigned as Green Standard brigade and garrison officers.
translations.idiomatic: If full payout at once is impossible, disburse over several years; reassign banner officers from commanders down to senior clerks as Green Standard brigade and garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 此安頓漢軍之法也。

translations.literal: This is the method for settling the Han Banners.
translations.idiomatic: This is how to settle the Han Banners.

sentences.zh: 臣又按耗羨歸公，天下之大利，亦天下之大弊也。

translations.literal: Your subject further notes that returning surplus melt fees to the public treasury is a great benefit to the realm and also a great harm to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I further observe that consolidating surplus melt fees into the public treasury is both the empire's greatest fiscal gain and its greatest administrative ill.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，法制寬略，州縣於地丁外私徵火耗，其陋規匿稅亦未盡釐剔。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi era institutions were lenient and broad; counties and prefectures privately levied melt fees beyond land and poll tax, and corrupt customary fees and hidden taxes were not fully swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, rules were loose; local officials still levied melt surcharges beyond land and poll taxes, and hidden customary fees were not fully eliminated.

sentences.zh: 自耗羨歸公，一切弊竇悉滌而清之，是為大利。

translations.literal: Since surplus melt fees were returned to the public treasury, every corrupt loophole was washed clean—that was the great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Once melt surcharges were centralized, corrupt channels were cleared—that was the gain.

sentences.zh: 然向者本出私徵，非同經費，其端介有司，不肯妄取，上司亦不敢強，賢且能者則以地方之財治地方之事，故康熙間循吏多實績可紀，而財用亦得流通。

translations.literal: Yet formerly these came from private levies, not regular appropriations; upright officials would not take them rashly and superiors dared not force them; the worthy and capable used local wealth to handle local affairs, so in Kangxi many honest officials had real achievements on record and funds also circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly such funds were informal levies, not budget lines; upright magistrates would not abuse them and superiors dared not demand them; capable men used local money for local needs, so Kangxi produced many honest officials with real achievements and fluid finances.

sentences.zh: 自耗羨歸公，輸納比於正供，出入操於內部，地丁公費，除官吏養廉無餘剩；

translations.literal: Since surplus melt fees were returned to the public treasury, payments were made like regular tribute and disbursements were controlled by the Board of Revenue; from land-poll tax and public expenses, aside from officials' integrity stipends nothing remained;
translations.idiomatic: After consolidation, payments matched regular tribute and the Board of Revenue controlled every outlay; beyond integrity stipends from land tax and public funds, nothing remained;

sentences.zh: 官吏養廉，除分給幕客家丁修脯工資，及事上接下之應酬，輿馬蔬薪之繁費，亦無餘剩。

translations.literal: officials' integrity stipends, aside from shares for secretaries, household servants, teachers' salaries, and wages, and the obligatory courtesies for superiors and subordinates, carriage, horse, vegetable, and firewood expenses—also nothing remained.
translations.idiomatic: integrity stipends, after secretaries, servants, teachers, wages, obligatory courtesies, and carriage and household costs, also left nothing.

sentences.zh: 地方有應行之事、應興之役，一絲一忽取公帑，有司上畏戶、工二部之駁詰，下畏身家之賠累，但取其事之美觀而無實濟者，日奔走之以為勤。

translations.literal: When the locality had matters that should be done and projects that should be undertaken, taking every thread and hair from the public treasury, officials feared rejection from the Boards of Revenue and Works above and personal ruin below; they only took what made the affair look fine without real benefit and ran about it daily as diligence.
translations.idiomatic: When local projects required funding, officials feared Board rejection above and personal liability below; they pursued showy projects without real benefit and called daily bustle diligence.

sentences.zh: 故曰天下之大弊也。

translations.literal: Thus it is called a great harm to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Hence it became a great ill for the empire.

sentences.zh: 夫生民之利有窮，故聖人之法必改。

translations.literal: The benefit to the people has limits, therefore the sages' laws must change.
translations.idiomatic: Public benefit has its limits; even sage institutions must adapt.

sentences.zh: 今耗羨歸公之法勢無可改，惟有為地方別立一公項，俾任事者無財用窘乏之患，而後可課以治效之成。

translations.literal: Now the law of returning surplus melt fees to the public treasury cannot in trend be changed; only establish a separate public fund for localities so those in charge have no worry of financial shortage, and then one can demand real administrative results.
translations.idiomatic: The melt-fee consolidation cannot be reversed; only a separate local public fund can spare responsible officials financial paralysis, so that real governance can be required of them.

sentences.zh: 臣請將常平倉儲仍照舊例辦理，捐監一項留充各省公用，除官俸兵餉動用正項，餘若災傷當拯卹，孤貧當養贍，河渠水利當興修，貧民開墾當借給工本，壇廟、祠宇、橋樑、公廨當修治，採買倉穀價值不敷，皆於此動給，以地方之財，治地方之事。

translations.literal: Your subject asks that ever-normal granary reserves still be handled by the old rules; the purchase-for-student item be retained to fill each province's public funds; aside from official salaries and troop pay which use regular items, the rest—when disaster and injury need relief, orphans and poor need support, rivers and waterworks need repair, poor people opening wasteland need seed loans, altars, temples, bridges, and government buildings need repair, and purchase of granary grain when prices fall short—all shall be drawn from this, using local wealth to handle local affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Keep ever-normal granaries under the old rules; dedicate student-purchase fees to provincial public funds; beyond salaries and troop pay from regular revenue, use this pool for disaster relief, poor relief, hydraulics, reclamation loans, public works, and grain purchases when prices fall short—local funds for local needs.

sentences.zh: 如有大役大費，則督撫合全省而通融之；

translations.literal: If there are great projects and great expenses, then governors-general and governors shall pool the whole province and adjust flexibly;
translations.idiomatic: For major projects, governors-general and governors should pool provincial resources;

sentences.zh: 又有不足，則移鄰省而協濟之。

translations.literal: if still insufficient, then shift from neighboring provinces to assist mutually.
translations.idiomatic: if still insufficient, neighboring provinces should mutual aid.

sentences.zh: 稽察屬司道，核減屬督撫，內部不必重加切核，則經費充裕，節目疏闊，而地方之實政皆可舉行。

translations.literal: Investigation belongs to the circuit and prefectural officials; reduction and verification belong to governors-general and governors; the Board of Revenue need not add heavy scrutiny—then funds will be ample, categories broad, and real local administration can all be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit and prefectural officials should audit use; governors-general and governors should approve reductions; the Board need not micromanage—then funds will suffice, rules stay simple, and genuine local policy can proceed.

sentences.zh: 設官分職，付以人民，只可立法以懲貪，不可因噎而廢食。

translations.literal: Establish offices and divide duties, entrusting them with the people—one can only legislate to punish greed, not stop eating for fear of choking.
translations.idiomatic: Offices exist to serve the people; write laws against corruption, but do not abolish necessary funds for fear of abuse.

sentences.zh: 唐人減劉晏之船料，而漕運不繼；

translations.literal: Tang men reduced Liu Yan's shipping fees and grain transport did not continue;
translations.idiomatic: Tang officials cut Liu Yan's shipping allowances and the grain transport system collapsed;

sentences.zh: 明人以周忱之耗米歸為正項，致逋負百出，路多飢殍。

translations.literal: Ming men made Zhou Chen's melt-rice surcharges into regular items, causing arrears everywhere and roads full of starving corpses.
translations.idiomatic: Ming officials converted Zhou Chen's transport surcharges into regular tax, spawning arrears everywhere and starving dead along the roads.

sentences.zh: 大國不可以小道治，善理財者，固不如此。

translations.literal: A great state cannot be governed by petty methods; those who manage wealth well are surely not like this.
translations.idiomatic: A great empire cannot be run by penny-wise tricks; sound fiscal statesmen do not act so.

sentences.zh: 此捐監之宜充公費也。

translations.literal: This is why purchase-for-student funds should fill public expenses.
translations.idiomatic: This is why student-purchase fees should fund provincial public expenses.

sentences.zh: 三法既行，則度支有定，經費有資，當今要務，無急於此者。

translations.literal: Once the three methods are enacted, then revenue and expenditure will be fixed and funds assured; among present urgent tasks none is more pressing than this.
translations.idiomatic: Once these three measures take effect, revenue and spending will stabilize and funds will be secure; no present task is more urgent.

sentences.zh: 伏乞皇上深留睿慮，敕公忠有識大臣，詳議施行。」

translations.literal: Your subject humbly begs the Emperor to ponder deeply, instruct loyal and knowledgeable ministers, and discuss and implement in detail."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to reflect deeply and charge loyal, capable ministers to deliberate and enact these proposals."

sentences.zh: 尋遷兵科給事中，巡視北城。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs and inspected the northern city.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs and assigned to inspect the northern city ward.

sentences.zh: 乞歸侍母，孝養肫至。

translations.literal: He begged leave to return and serve his mother, filial in nurture to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave to care for his mother and nursed her with devoted filial piety.

sentences.zh: 貧，以醫自給。

translations.literal: Poor, he supported himself by practicing medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In poverty he supported himself as a physician.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After long time, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In time he died.

sentences.zh: 儲麟趾，字履醇，江南荊溪人。

translations.literal: Chu Linzhi, style name Lüchun, a man of Jingxi in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Linzhi, courtesy name Lüchun, was a native of Jingxi in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1739 he passed the jinshi examination, became a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 進諸經講義，援據儒先，責難陳善，辭旨醇美。

translations.literal: Presenting commentaries on the classics, he cited earlier Confucians, pressed difficult questions and offered good counsel; his wording was pure and fine.
translations.idiomatic: In presenting classical commentaries he drew on the ancients, posed sharp questions, and offered constructive criticism in language of refined clarity.

sentences.zh: 十四年，考選貴州道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was selected and appointed supervising censor of the Guizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1749 he was selected and appointed supervising censor for the Guizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 編修硃荃與大學士張廷玉有連，督四川學政，母死發喪緩。

translations.literal: Compiler Zhu Quan was connected by marriage to Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu; as educational commissioner of Sichuan he was slow to begin mourning when his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: The compiler Zhu Quan was related by marriage to Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu; while serving as educational commissioner of Sichuan he delayed observing mourning when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 麟趾疏劾，語不避廷玉，高宗以是知其伉直。

translations.literal: Linzhi memorialized to impeach him, his words not avoiding Tingyu; the Gaozong Emperor thereby knew his blunt uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Linzhi submitted a memorial impeaching him without sparing Zhang Tingyu's name; Emperor Gaozong took this as proof of his blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 嘗大旱，麟趾應詔上疏，略言：「臣聞天道若持衡然。

translations.literal: Once during a great drought, Linzhi responded to an imperial edict with a memorial, saying in summary: 'Your subject has heard that the Way of Heaven is like holding a balance level.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought he answered an imperial call for memorials with a submission that, in essence, said: "Your subject has heard that Heaven's way is like keeping a steelyard in balance.

sentences.zh: 故雨暘寒燠，無時不得其平；

translations.literal: Thus rain and sunshine, cold and warmth—at no time fail to find their equilibrium;
translations.idiomatic: Rain and sun, cold and heat—each in its season finds its proper mean;

sentences.zh: 而氣化偶偏，必於亢陽伏陰示其像。

translations.literal: yet when the transformation of qi happens to skew, it must show its sign in blazing yang and hidden yin.
translations.idiomatic: yet when the cosmic breath momentarily tilts, the sign appears in excessive yang suppressed beneath yin.

sentences.zh: 然往來推行，久而必復其常者，天道之無私也。

translations.literal: Yet in coming and going and rolling on, in time it must return to the norm—that is the impartiality of Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Still, as cycles turn and time passes, balance always returns—that is Heaven's impartiality.

sentences.zh: 君道法天，亦若持衡然。

translations.literal: The ruler's Way follows Heaven, likewise as if holding a balance level.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's way mirrors Heaven, likewise as though holding a steelyard level.

sentences.zh: 故喜怒刑賞，無事不得其平；

translations.literal: Thus joy and anger, punishment and reward—in all affairs not failing to find their equilibrium;
translations.idiomatic: Joy and anger, punishment and reward—in governance nothing should stray from the mean;

sentences.zh: 而意見偶偏，必於用人行政露其機。

translations.literal: yet when opinion happens to skew, it must reveal its mechanism in the employment of men and conduct of administration.
translations.idiomatic: yet when judgment slips, the tell appears in whom you appoint and how you rule.

sentences.zh: 然斟酌損益，終必歸於大中至正者，君德之極盛也。

translations.literal: Yet through weighing and adding or subtracting, in the end one must return to the great mean and utmost rightness—that is the fullest flourishing of the ruler's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Through careful adjustment, all must finally settle on the great mean and perfect rectitude—that is the height of royal virtue.

sentences.zh: 漢臣董仲舒曰：'善言天者，必有驗於人，天人相應，捷於桴鼓。

translations.literal: Han official Dong Zhongshu said: 'Those who speak well of Heaven must find verification in men; Heaven and man respond to each other, swifter than drumstick and drum.
translations.idiomatic: The Han scholar Dong Zhongshu said, 'Those who speak truly of Heaven prove it in human affairs; Heaven and humanity answer each other faster than stick strikes drum.

sentences.zh: 春秋所以詳書災異也。

translations.literal: That is why the Spring and Autumn Annals records calamities and anomalies in detail.'
translations.idiomatic: That is why the Spring and Autumn Annals records disasters and portents at length.'

sentences.zh: '皇上至聖極明，豈復有纖芥之事足以召祲而致災者？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is utterly sage and supremely clear—could there still be any matter however slight enough to summon omens and bring calamity?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is utterly sage and penetratingly wise—surely no trifling fault could summon ill omens and bring disaster?

sentences.zh: 但愚臣蠡測管窺，以為自古人主患不明，惟皇上患明之太過；

translations.literal: But this foolish subject, measuring with a gourd dipper and peering through a bamboo tube, thinks that from antiquity rulers have worried about not being clear, whereas Your Majesty alone worries about being too clear;
translations.idiomatic: Yet your foolish subject, guessing with a dipper and peering through a tube, believes that ancient rulers feared being unclear, whereas Your Majesty alone fears being too clear;

sentences.zh: 自古人主患不斷，惟皇上患斷之太速。

translations.literal: from antiquity rulers have worried about not being decisive, whereas Your Majesty alone worries about being too quick to decide.
translations.idiomatic: ancient rulers feared indecision, whereas Your Majesty alone fears deciding too swiftly.

sentences.zh: 即如擢一官、點一差，往往出人意表，為擬議所不及。

translations.literal: Even promoting one official or assigning one post—often it is beyond what people expect, beyond what deliberation could reach.
translations.idiomatic: Even a single promotion or appointment often surprises everyone, beyond what deliberation could anticipate.

sentences.zh: 此則皇上意見之稍偏，而愚臣所謂聖明英斷之太過者也。

translations.literal: This then is a slight bias in Your Majesty's views—what your foolish subject calls excess of sagely clarity and resolute decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: This is the slight tilt in Your Majesty's judgment—what I mean by an excess of sagely clarity and swift decisiveness.

sentences.zh: 史臣之贊堯曰：'乃聖乃神。'

translations.literal: The historiographer's praise of Yao says: 'Then sage, then divine.'
translations.idiomatic: The historians' praise of Yao reads, 'Sage upon sage, spirit upon spirit.'

sentences.zh: 宋儒硃子曰：'聖人，神明不測之號。'

translations.literal: Song Confucian Master Zhu said: 'The sage—the title of spirit so unfathomable.'
translations.idiomatic: The Song master Zhu Xi said, 'The sage is the name for one whose spirit cannot be fathomed.'

sentences.zh: 夫所貴乎不測者，錯綜參伍，與時偕行，而非於彼於此不可思議之謂也。

translations.literal: What is prized in "unfathomable" is weaving together and comparing in array, advancing with the times—not meaning incomprehensible in this or that particular.
translations.idiomatic: What is admirable in "unfathomable" is weaving many strands together, weighing them in array, and moving with the times—not meaning inexplicable in this matter or that.

sentences.zh: 此雖不足上累聖德萬分之一，然臣尤原皇上開誠佈公，太和翔洽，要使天下服皇上用人之至當，不必徒使天下驚皇上用人之甚奇。

translations.literal: This though it cannot diminish Your Majesty's sacred virtue by one ten-thousandth, yet your subject especially hopes Your Majesty will open sincerity and spread fairness, with supreme harmony soaring in accord, so as to make the realm accept Your Majesty's appointments as utterly fitting—not merely to startle the realm with how strange Your Majesty's appointments are.
translations.idiomatic: This can hardly touch Your Majesty's virtue by one part in ten thousand, yet your subject especially wishes that Your Majesty would open your heart and act with perfect fairness, so that harmony pervades the realm and the world admires the rightness of your appointments—not merely marvels at how startling they are.

sentences.zh: 若云防微杜漸，不得不爾，則國法具在，試問諸臣行事邪正，又誰能欺皇上之洞鑑者？

translations.literal: If one says that to guard against the subtle and stop the gradual one must act thus—then the laws of the state stand complete; ask whether officials' conduct is crooked or straight—who could deceive Your Majesty's penetrating mirror?
translations.idiomatic: If the answer is that one must do so to nip trouble in the bud, the laws of the realm are already complete; tell me which minister's conduct is crooked or straight—who could hide anything from Your Majesty's penetrating gaze?

sentences.zh: 抑臣又聞之，唐臣韓愈曰：'獨陽為旱，獨陰為水。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject has also heard: Tang official Han Yu said: 'Yang alone makes drought, yin alone makes flood.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has also heard the Tang minister Han Yu say, 'Yang alone brings drought, yin alone brings flood.

sentences.zh: 君陽臣陰，有君無臣，是以久旱。

translations.literal: The ruler is yang, ministers are yin; where there is a ruler but no ministers, hence prolonged drought.'
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is yang and ministers are yin; where there is a ruler but no ministers, drought persists.'

sentences.zh: '今皇上宵衣旰食，焦勞於法宮之中，而王公大臣拱手備位，不聞出其謀畫，上贊主德，輔宣聖化。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, rising early and retiring late, toils anxious in the inner palace, while princes and great ministers fold their hands and fill their posts, without hearing them offer their plans, exalt the ruler's virtue on high, or assist in proclaiming sagely transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Today Your Majesty rises before dawn and retires after dark, worn with care within the palace, while princes and grand ministers stand with folded hands filling their seats, offering no counsel, doing nothing to magnify your virtue or help spread your sage rule.

sentences.zh: 是君勞於上，臣逸於下，天道下濟而地道不能上行。

translations.literal: This is the ruler laboring above while ministers rest below—Heaven's way descends to bestow while Earth's way cannot ascend.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler toils above while ministers idle below—Heaven's bounty flows downward while Earth's response cannot rise.

sentences.zh: 其於致旱，理或宜然。

translations.literal: As for causing drought, it may well be that the principle fits.
translations.idiomatic: As a cause of drought, the logic may well hold.

sentences.zh: 臣區區之忱，原皇上虛中無我，一切用人行政，不改鑑空衡平之體。

translations.literal: Your subject's humble sincerity hopes Your Majesty will empty the mind and be without self—in all employment of men and conduct of administration, not altering the substance of mirror-empty and balance-level.
translations.idiomatic: In all humility your subject wishes that Your Majesty would empty the self and hold no private bias—in every appointment and every policy keep the even mirror and level balance unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又於一二純誠憂國之大臣，時賜召對，清宴之餘，資其輔益。

translations.literal: And toward one or two utterly sincere ministers who worry for the state, from time to time grant them audiences; in the leisure after a pure banquet, draw on their supplementary benefit.
translations.idiomatic: And toward one or two ministers of pure loyalty who fret for the realm, summon them now and then; in quiet moments after a simple repast, draw on their counsel.

sentences.zh: 必能時雨時風，消殄旱災矣。」

translations.literal: Then timely rain and timely wind will surely extinguish the drought disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Then timely rain and wind will surely dispel the drought."

translations.literal: (Close of memorial quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of memorial.)

sentences.zh: 麟趾累遷太僕寺卿，移宗人府府丞。

translations.literal: Linzhi was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then transferred to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Linzhi rose through several posts to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then became vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 引疾歸，家居十餘年。

translations.literal: He cited illness and returned home, living at home for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and retired, remaining at home for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 論曰：諫臣之益人國，最上匡君德，次則綢繆軍國，洞百年之利害。

translations.literal: The discussion says: The benefit remonstrating ministers give the state—at the highest they correct the ruler's virtue, next they plan military and state affairs in detail, penetrating a century's benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion: The historians observe that remonstrating ministers serve the state best when they rectify the ruler's virtue, next when they plan military and civil affairs and grasp a century's worth of gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 若夫擊邪毖患，岳岳不避權要，固亦有不易言者。

translations.literal: As for striking at evil and guarding against harm, stern and not avoiding the powerful—in that too there are those not easily spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: As for striking down wickedness and shutting out harm, standing tall and not flinching before the powerful—that too demands courage not easily praised in words.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣服，虛己納諫。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, he emptied himself to receive remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne, he humbled himself to accept remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 一士、慎修、潮生、麟趾，其所獻替，合陳善責難之誼。

translations.literal: Yishi, Shenxiu, Chaosheng, and Linzhi—their offered replacements accorded with the propriety of presenting good and demanding difficult questions.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yishi, Li Shenxiu, Chai Chaosheng, and Chu Linzhi—the counsel they offered fulfilled the duty of presenting good and pressing hard questions.

sentences.zh: 潮生所論理財三策尤閎遠，惜不能用也。

translations.literal: Chaosheng's three policies on managing finances were especially broad and far-reaching—pity they could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Chaosheng's three policies on public finance were especially far-sighted—a pity they were never adopted.

sentences.zh: 定劾許容，永檀彈鄂善，皆能舉其職者。

translations.literal: Ding impeaching Xu Rong, Yongtan impeaching E Shan—all were able to fulfill their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ding's impeachment of Xu Rong and Zhong Yongtan's impeachment of E Shan both showed men who could perform their offices.

sentences.zh: 永檀乃以漏言敗，異哉！

translations.literal: Yet Yongtan ruined himself through leaked words—how strange!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yongtan destroyed himself through a leak of words—how strange!
